#2246. Calciomercato no stop - Indiscrezioni, trattative e retroscena del 3 novembre

INTER, ALL'OPERA PER I RINNOVI DI DIMARCO, CALHANOGLU E THURAM. JUVENTUS, IL RETROSCENA DI GREGORIO-MANDAS. LAZIO, SIRENE DALLA PREMIER LEAGUE PER TAYLOR. FROSINONE, PRONTO A QUINTUPLICARE L'INGAGGIO DI KVERNADZE. SASSUOLO, LIPANI RINNOVA E PER LAURIENTÈ NON MANCANO GLI ESTIMATORI IN INGHILTERRA

BOLOGNA Il Bologna guarda al futuro e monitora con interesse la crescita di Motiejus Sapola, difensore centrale lituano classe 2006 di proprietà del Pisa, attualmente in prestito allo Spezia, capolista imbattuto del Girone B di Serie C. Le prestazioni del giovane, che potrebbe anche ricevere la convocazione della nazionale maggiore per gli impegni di Nations League di novembre, hanno attirato l'attenzione di diversi club di categoria superiore. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Secolo XIX, oltre al Frosinone anche il Bologna segue il centrale in vista della stagione 2027/28, individuato come un possibile rinforzo giovane e fisicamente strutturato per la retroguardia. Il Pisa, che crede nelle qualità del giocatore, ha fissato un riscatto a 800 mila euro, mantenendo un diritto di controriscatto a 200 mila: cifre che potrebbero però aumentare qualora l'interesse della Serie A diventasse più concreto.

FROSINONE Il Frosinone lavora su più fronti, tra il presente e le prospettive del mercato. La priorità riguarda Giorgi Kvernadze, protagonista di un ottimo avvio di stagione con tre gol e quattro assist in dieci giornate: il club di Stirpe è pronto a proporgli un rinnovo fino a circa un milione di euro a stagione, cinque volte l'attuale ingaggio, per blindarlo ed evitare che possa finire sul mercato già a gennaio, considerando il contratto in scadenza nel 2028 e l'interesse di diverse società. Intanto emerge un retroscena di mercato su Gustavo Varela, oggi al Monza e capocannoniere della Serie B con nove reti: la scorsa estate il Frosinone aveva raggiunto un accordo con il Benfica per acquistarlo a 2,5 milioni di euro, con il 50% sulla futura rivendita, salvo poi scegliere Tomas Bobcek, arrivato dal Lechia Danzica per 11 milioni. Sul fronte delle possibili uscite, invece, Francesco Gelli potrebbe lasciare i ciociari a gennaio dopo essere finito ai margini della prima squadra: sulle sue tracce c'è lo Spezia di Guido Angelozzi, che lo aveva portato in giallazzurro nel 2023. Infine, proprio lo Spezia potrebbe rappresentare un'opportunità anche per il futuro: il club ligure, attraverso il lavoro di Angelozzi, segue Motiejus Sapola, difensore classe 2006 di proprietà del Pisa, che interessa anche al Bologna in vista della stagione 2027/28.

INTER L'Inter è al lavoro su più fronti per definire il futuro della propria rosa, con diversi dossier contrattuali aperti. Per Federico Dimarco, dopo l'esercizio dell'opzione fino al 2028, sono previsti nei prossimi giorni contatti con i nuovi agenti per discutere un adeguamento dell'ingaggio e un prolungamento a lungo termine, con la volontà comune di proseguire insieme. Procede spedita anche la trattativa per il rinnovo di Carlos Augusto, mentre per Marcus Thuram ogni discorso è rimandato a un secondo momento. Più delicata la situazione di Hakan Çalhanoğlu, in scadenza a giugno e senza opzioni automatiche: il turco vorrebbe un biennale per restare a Milano, ma sullo sfondo ci sono interessamenti dalla Turchia e altre possibili destinazioni. Sul fronte del mercato, invece, torna d'attualità il nome di Lisandro Martinez: il Manchester United starebbe valutando una possibile cessione a gennaio e l'Inter, insieme a Roma e Como, osserva con attenzione gli sviluppi, considerando l'opportunità di riportare in Serie A il centrale argentino. Infine, uno sguardo al futuro delle corsie esterne: piace nuovamente Givairo Read, talento classe 2006 del Feyenoord già seguito in estate dopo l'addio di Dumfries. Il club olandese aveva respinto anche un'offerta della Roma da circa 30 milioni di euro, ma il rendimento del giovane esterno, autore di sei assist in undici gare di Eredivisie, continua a convincere.

JUVENTUS La vittoria contro il Napoli rappresenta un primo passo importante nel percorso di ripartenza della Juventus, ma la dirigenza è consapevole che restano diverse situazioni da sistemare e guarda già al mercato di gennaio. La priorità è un terzino sinistro che possa affiancare Andrea Cambiaso: sul taccuino ci sono David Raum del Lipsia, Rayan Ait-Nouri del Manchester City e Mahamadou Nagida del Rennes. Attenzione anche al centrocampo, dove Teun Koopmeiners non è considerato incedibile e tra i profili valutati spicca Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg del Marsiglia. Si ragiona inoltre su un possibile intervento in attacco: tra i nomi accostati ai bianconeri figurano Folarin Balogun, Alexander Sorloth e Mauro Icardi, ma un eventuale acquisto richiederebbe anche una cessione, con Edon Zhegrova tra i possibili partenti. Intanto emerge un retroscena della scorsa estate: la Juventus aveva valutato seriamente Christos Mandas, portiere della Lazio protagonista di un ottimo avvio di stagione con quattro clean sheet in undici presenze, prendendo in considerazione anche uno scambio con Michele Di Gregorio. L'operazione non si concretizzò per la volontà di Gennaro Gattuso di puntare sul greco, il cui valore oggi viene stimato tra i 20 e i 25 milioni di euro. Sul fronte dei giovani, infine, arriva una notizia ufficiale: Destiny Elimoghale, esterno offensivo classe 2009 già aggregato alla Juventus Next Gen, ha rinnovato il contratto fino al 30 giugno 2029, confermando la volontà del club di investire sul suo percorso di crescita.

LAZIO La Lazio si gode il primato in classifica e lavora contemporaneamente per blindare i suoi protagonisti. Tra questi c'è Kenneth Taylor, centrocampista olandese arrivato dall'Ajax nel gennaio 2026 per un'operazione da 17 milioni di euro bonus compresi, che ha già attirato l'interesse della Premier League: Brighton e Bournemouth hanno effettuato i primi sondaggi dopo un avvio di stagione da due gol e due assist in dieci presenze. La società biancoceleste non ha intenzione di privarsene a gennaio, ma dovrà prestare attenzione ai possibili sviluppi in vista dell'estate. Intanto sono iniziati i contatti per il rinnovo di Gustav Isaksen, il cui contratto scade nel 2028: l'obiettivo è prolungare almeno fino al 2030, accompagnando l'accordo con un adeguamento economico, dopo la crescita dell'esterno danese, già autore di quattro reti in dieci giornate. Tra le note più positive c'è anche Christos Mandas, protagonista di un ottimo rendimento con quattro clean sheet in undici presenze e dieci gol subiti. Il portiere greco, acquistato dall'OFI Creta per appena 951mila euro, oggi ha una valutazione stimata tra i 20 e i 25 milioni. La scorsa estate la Juventus aveva provato a inserirlo in un possibile scambio con Michele Di Gregorio, ma Gennaro Gattuso ha voluto trattenerlo a Roma, puntando su di lui come titolare: una scelta che sta dando ampiamente ragione all'allenatore.

MONZA Il Monza si gode l'esplosione di Gustavo Varela, attaccante portoghese arrivato in estate dal Benfica e attualmente capocannoniere della Serie B con nove reti in dieci presenze, una in più rispetto ad Antonio Raimondo, ora costretto a fermarsi per qualche settimana a causa di un infortunio. Intanto emerge un retroscena di mercato raccolto da Tuttomercatoweb.com: la scorsa estate Varela era stato molto vicino al Frosinone, che aveva raggiunto un accordo con il Benfica per acquistarlo a 2,5 milioni di euro, lasciando al club portoghese il 50% sulla futura rivendita. I ciociari avevano però successivamente scelto di puntare su Tomas Bobcek, arrivato dal Lechia Danzica per 11 milioni. A quel punto si è inserito il Monza, che ha chiuso l'operazione per circa 2 milioni più bonus, riconoscendo al Benfica il 20% sulla futura rivendita e un diritto di prelazione: in caso di un'offerta ufficiale da parte di un altro club, i lusitani potranno infatti pareggiarla e riportare il giocatore in patria.

SASSUOLO Il Sassuolo guarda al futuro e blinda Luca Lipani: il centrocampista classe 2005 ha firmato un rinnovo quinquennale che lo legherà al club neroverde fino al 30 giugno 2031, confermando la volontà della società di puntare sui giovani talenti nonostante il difficile avvio di stagione. Intanto resta aperto il capitolo Armand Laurienté, ancora uno dei principali uomini mercato della formazione emiliana. L'esterno francese, sotto contratto fino al 2029, continua a essere seguito in Italia e all'estero: in estate si erano mosse l'Ipswich Town e diverse società turche, tra cui Fenerbahce, Besiktas e Trabzonspor, senza però raggiungere la valutazione di almeno 25 milioni di euro fissata dal Sassuolo. Anche il Napoli potrebbe tornare a interessarsi al giocatore, già inserito nella propria lista durante la scorsa sessione invernale. La posizione ufficiale del club, attraverso il ds Francesco Palmieri, è quella di non voler cedere i propri giocatori a gennaio, ma l'interesse per Laurienté potrebbe comunque riaccendere le trattative in vista del mercato invernale.

FONSECA È TORNATO IN PORTOGALLO: ADDIO LIONE, QUESTIONE DI ORE L'ANNUNCIO CON LO SPORTING LISBONA. FABIO CANNAVARO PUO' LASCIARE LA PANCHINA DELL'UZBEKISTAN. COSA SUCCEDE AL FENERBAHCE: SERGIO CONCEICAO NON ARRIVA. NUNO ESPIRITO SANTO ESONERATO DAL WEST HAM.

Paulo Fonseca è sbarcato all'aeroporto Humberto Delgado di Lisbona per formalizzare il suo passaggio allo Sporting, pronto a raccogliere l'eredità di Rui Borges ad Alvalade dopo aver risolto gli ultimi dettagli contrattuali per l'addio al Lione. L'ex tecnico del Milan, che ha salutato tra le lacrime i gones al termine della vittoria per 2-0 sull'Angers in Ligue 1, ha espresso la propria felicità per il ritorno in patria, rimandando ogni approfondimento ai prossimi giorni. Nella giornata di mercoledì, con il rientro dall'Inghilterra del presidente del club lusitano Frederico Varandas, si procederà alla firma del contratto che legherà il cinquantatreenne alla società lusitana fino al 2030 con un ingaggio da 3 milioni di euro netti a stagione, mentre nelle casse dell'OL andrà un indennizzo pari a 5 milioni di euro per liberare l'allenatore.

Si appresta a vivere uno snodo cruciale l'esperienza di Fabio Cannavaro alla guida dell'Uzbekistan, con l'ex Pallone d'oro pronto a rassegnare le dimissioni da commissario tecnico a causa del rinvio di quasi un anno della Coppa d'Asia 2027, come svelato da Fabrizio Romano. Subentrato nell'ottobre 2025 a Timur Kapadze - l'uomo che aveva condotto la selezione al suo primo storico pass per i Mondiali 2026 -, l'ex difensore di Inter e Juventus ha subito avvertito il peso della responsabilità, assumendosi la paternità dell'eliminazione rimediata la scorsa estate con tre sconfitte nella fase a gironi del torneo iridato, pur rimarcando la crescita maturata dalla squadra su scala globale. Resta ora da capire se sarà ancora lui a dirigere gli uzbeki nei test internazionali programmati per il mese di novembre contro Russia e Arabia Saudita.

Fumata nera in casa Fenerbahce per l'approdo in panchina di Sergio Conceiçao. Nonostante l'intesa totale non fosse ancora stata raggiunta, la trattativa sembrava incanalata verso la fumata bianca, ma il tavolo negoziale è saltato improvvisamente nella notte: il club di Istanbul ha giudicato eccessive le pretese salariali avanzate dall'ex allenatore del Milan, scegliendo di virare con decisione su un profilo autoctono. Nel mirino dei gialloblù è così finito Emre Belozoglu, autentica bandiera della società con tre differenti parentesi da calciatore (2008-12, 2013-15 e 2019/20) e un'esperienza da tecnico avviata proprio al Fener nel 2021 dopo l'esonero di Erol Bulut. L'operazione per riportare a casa l'ex centrocampista dell'Inter presenta tuttavia un ostacolo di mercato: Emre è attualmente vincolato al Kasimpasa - quinto in classifica a quota 17 punti dopo 10 giornate -, costringendo il Fenerbahçe a trattare la liberazione del tecnico dietro il pagamento di un indennizzo ai rivali di campionato.

Termina l'esperienza di Nuno Espirito Santo sulla panchina del West Ham. Il tecnico portoghese, alla guida del club londinese dal settembre del 2025, è stato esonerato dal club dopo la brutta partenza in Championship (la seconda divisione inglese) con l'ottavo posto e appena 22 punti conquistati in 13 presenze. Il West Ham United conferma che l'allenatore della prima squadra maschile, Nuno Espírito Santo, ha lasciato il suo incarico con effetto immediato. A seguito di un'attenta analisi dell'inizio di stagione dell'EFL Championship, il Consiglio di Amministrazione ritiene necessario un cambiamento per garantire che gli obiettivi del Club rimangano in linea con le aspettative. Anche l'assistente allenatore Rui Pedro Silva e l'allenatore dei portieri Rui Barbosa hanno lasciato lo staff. Il West Ham United desidera ringraziare Nuno, Rui e Rui per il loro impegno e la dedizione dimostrati durante la loro permanenza nel Club, e augura loro tutto il meglio per il futuro.

#2245. Brocchi: "La Lazio di Gattuso somiglia alla mia. Dove può arrivare? Vi dico che..."

Il primato in classifica e il momento straordinario che sta attraversando la Lazio di Gattuso non sono passati inosservati agli ex biancocelesti. In particolare, a parlarne è stato Cristian Brocchi sulle colonne de La Repubblica. L'ex centrocampista biancoceleste, protagonista della Lazio del 2010 di Reja, visse un inizio campionato molto simile a quello dell'attuale formazione laziale. Di seguito l'intervista.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

L’entusiasmo con cui questa squadra scende in campo, è lo stesso che avevamo noi. E anche allora eravamo reduci da una stagione difficile e sofferta, siamo stati capaci di trasformare negatività e scetticismo in energia positiva, proprio come questa Lazio. Nessuno voleva rivivere le sensazioni dell’anno prima. E poi il mercato. Nel gennaio precedente, parliamo del 2010, arrivarono giocatori importanti come Biava, Dias e Floccari, che si integrarono subito e sistemarono la squadra. Così siamo partiti, pochi mesi dopo, con uno spirito diverso e più certezze. Stessa cosa è successa con Taylor: arrivato a gennaio 2026, è uno dei perni della formazione di Gattuso, un grande calciatore.

Si rivede in qualche centrocampista della Lazio di oggi? Stimo molto Frattesi, che ho allenato al Monza. Dico sempre che dentro ha il 50% di Brocchi, cioè la mentalità vincente e la voglia di lottare, l’altro 50% è l’abilità in zona gol, che io non avevo. In tv, a inizio campionato, avevo detto che avrebbe potuto competere per l’Europa, perché ha giocatori di valore con caratteristiche adatte al calcio di Gattuso. Lui ha sempre creduto in questo gioco aggressivo, non è cambiato. Però ora non alziamo troppo l’asticella, a Roma è pericoloso, lo so bene, poi bastano un paio di passi falsi e subito si dice che è finita la magia o la benzina. Si passa dall’euforia allo sconforto in un attimo. È successo anche a noi, quando perdemmo il primo posto dopo le sconfitte nel derby e a Cesena. E a gennaio ricordo le polemiche perché ci si aspettava più rinforzi sul mercato (arrivò solo Sculli, ndr). Bisogna procedere partita dopo partita, con realismo, e reagire bene ai momenti negativi.

Obiettivi? Per come si sta esprimendo adesso, anche questa squadra può lottare per entrare tra le prime quattro: avevo previsto che si sarebbe classificata tra la sesta e l’ottava posizione, ora dico tra la quarta e la sesta. Il percorso però è lungo, le big sono più abituate a fare punti pesanti, impossibile sottovalutarle. E ci saranno tanti scontri diretti da affrontare. Ma se la Lazio sarà così in alto anche alla vigilia degli ultimi due mesi, allora tutto potrà succedere.

Gattuso? Ha rivitalizzato calciatori forti che non avevano reso secondo il loro valore. Penso in particolare a Tavares e Zaccagni: con Sarri, che considero comunque un grande allenatore, erano come leoni in gabbia, Rino li ha liberati e ora fanno la differenza. Anche Noslin, Isaksen e lo stesso Taylor rendono molto di più. Provstgaard non giocava, adesso è un titolare.

Ha un sogno, Gattuso? Conoscendolo, vorrebbe rivedere l’Olimpico pieno. Io sono molto legato al popolo biancoceleste, è fantastico: quando firmai per la Lazio ero felice perché da avversario ero incantato dall’atmosfera di quello stadio e finalmente sarebbe stato il mio campo. Quindi capisco il sogno di Rino, spero riesca a realizzarlo.

#2242. Falkirk confirm tragic death of lifelong supporter shortly after victory over Celtic

Falkirk have confirmed the tragic news that a lifelong supporter passed away shortly after the win over Celtic on Sunday.

The club issued a statement on Sunday night offering their "heartfelt condolences" to the family and friends of the man.

The supporter passed away shortly after leaving the stadium following the 2-0 win in the Scottish Premiership fixture.

Falkirk Football Club is aware that a lifelong supporter tragically passed away shortly after leaving today’s game. Everyone at Falkirk FC sends their heartfelt condolences to his family and friends at this most difficult time. https://t.co/LFB6IX2XCS

— Falkirk FC (@FalkirkFC) November 1, 2026

A Falkirk post on social media read: "Falkirk Football Club is aware that a lifelong supporter tragically passed away shortly after leaving today’s game.

"Everyone at Falkirk FC sends their heartfelt condolences to his family and friends at this most difficult time."

Falkirk claimed a 2-0 win in Sunday's Scottish Premiership tie, with Ethan Ross and Scott Tanser finding the net.

Scott Bain put in an outstanding display in goal to keep a clean sheet for Falkirk against his former club.

#2241. Attenti a dare per morta l’Inter. Roma: che torto a Manchester, ma Gasp lasci stare Baresi. Il vero errore di De Laurentiis: Napoli non è per i grandi gestori. Galliani-Malagò, quanti colpi bassi

La caccia al piccione sull’Inter di Cristian Chivu parte subito. È bastato un derby giocato oggettivamente male per far partire il processo, esterno e in parte interno - perché dei problemi ci sono - a una squadra che in Champions League è tornata a mostrare il suo lato feroce. A Rotterdam, i nerazzurri hanno mandato un messaggio: nonostante i jolly europei siano finiti, ci sono eccome. Quanto al campionato, al termine della scorsa edizione della Serie A l’Inter ha trionfato senza portare a casa quasi nessuno scontro diretto, sicuramente non i derby. Al netto di tutte le incertezze di una squadra che negli ultimi anni ha vinto meno di quello che poteva, e che sicuramente spesso si sopravvaluta rispetto all’avversario, è la continuità il segreto di questa formazione.

Quanto al mercato dei nerazzurri, si fa un gran parlare dell’eventuale quinta punta. Ci divertiamo anche noi, ma intanto Beppe Marotta ha - giustamente - chiuso a Mauro Icardi. E penso che non sia così scontato l’arrivo di un attaccante anche a gennaio. O meglio: avrebbe molto più senso puntare su un ragazzo. Nell’Under 23 forse non ce ne sono di pronti per reggere il ritmo, ma la seconda squadra - in teoria - serve a questo: con un parco attaccanti composto da Lautaro, Thuram, Esposito e Bonny, un ulteriore puntero giocherebbe comunque poco e nulla. Tanto vale dare spazio a un ragazzo che in C ha iniziato a farsi le ossa come, per esempio, Lavelli, già visto.

Tornando alla Champions: a Manchester si è vista una cosa brutta. Non tanto la prestazione sfortunata di Leonardo Balerdi, che pure finora ha fatto benissimo e Gian Piero Gasperini aveva paragonato - per caratteristiche, non valore assoluto - a Franco Baresi. Ecco: lasciamo perdere i paragoni, portano sfiga. La cosa peggiore è quel rigore ribattuto da Bruno Fernandes, per una porzione di spalla di Bryan Cristante in area. Il VAR non è intervenuto per correggere il clamoroso abbaglio dell'arbitro - Cunha cade già prima del presunto contatto con Mancini -, salvo poi consentire ai Red Devils il replay del penalty parato dal portiere giallorosso. E qui c'è bisogno che qualcosa ce la spieghino: o i monitor si accendono sempre o non si accendono mai, così è una sconfitta che lascia un retrogusto amarissimo.

La trasferta del Napoli in casa del Porto sarà lo scenario di un what if per Aurelio De Laurentiis: e se avesse puntato su Francesco Farioli? L’allenatore italiano è un vecchio pallino di ADL, che raramente, quando si è trattato di scegliere il manico, ha sbagliato, ma questa volta sembra di sì. La tentazione è dire che De Laurentiis abbia sbagliato scelta quando è andato sul sicuro: Massimiliano Allegri come Carlo Ancelotti, le due grandi delusioni - posto che poi Carletto s’è preso una rivincita mica da poco su chi pensava fosse finito - dell’era partenopea del produttore cinematografico. A questa impressione si potrebbe però obiettare che, in realtà, anche prendere Antonio Conte, al netto dei dubbi sul rapporto con la piazza (già affrontati però all’Inter), era andare sul sicuro. E che non lo era mica tanto con Rudi Garcia, altro macro errore. Allora, forse, il punto è un altro.

C’entra la squadra: quella attuale ha bisogno di andare a mille all’ora, come faceva con Conte. Con Allegri, che s’è rintanato nella sua immagine di tecnico anti-calcio, questo non succede. C’entra, forse ancora di più, la piazza. Nelle sue meraviglie e contraddizioni, Napoli è la città di Masaniello e mica di Cavour. Napoli, a costo di essere banali, vive di grandi emozioni e non di chi vuole gestire quelle che già ci sono. È un cortocircuito che forse De Laurentiis ha mal considerato, e chissà che quella passione non avrebbe saputo nutrirla meglio lo stesso Farioli o, perché no, quel Vincenzo Italiano su cui, nonostante tanto facesse pensare a lui come uomo giusto, ADL non ha avuto il coraggio di puntare.

È agli sgoccioli la prima fase della lunghissima campagna elettorale tra Adriano Galliani e Giovanni Malagò. Mancano però 40 giorni all’elezione del prossimo presidente federale e saranno molto intensi. Anche nel modo più deteriore del termine, dato che questa partita si gioca anche a base di colpi bassi. Questione di nomine e di ombre (improbabili) di conflitti di potere, doppie firme e un regolamento di conti che rischia di lasciare strascichi pesanti anche quando la FIGC avrà finalmente un nuovo presidente. È una vicenda che, se continuerà su questa falsariga, rischia di spaccare il calcio italiano molto più a lungo di quanto non sembri. E adesso partirà uno squalificante mercatino dei voti. Nel frattempo, di sostanza e contenuti, ci pare ci sia davvero poco, per non dire praticamente nulla. È un gran peccato.

#2239. Celtic handed fresh agony as star who got away rewrites Eredivisie record books

Sizzling Sondre Orjaester tore up the Eredivisie record books on Sunday and handed Celtic an unwanted reminder of the winger who slipped through their grasp.

The Norwegian wide man was the star of the show as FC Twente demolished Excelsior 9-0, chalking up an astonishing FIVE assists in the rout. The remarkable haul is the highest assist tally recorded by a player in a single Eredivisie match this century and underlines the stunning form that has made Orjaester one of the hottest properties in Dutch football.

It's another painful "what if?" moment for Celtic as the Premiership champions continue to search for answers in a difficult campaign.

The Parkhead club kept close tabs on the former Sarpsborg flyer and pushed to land him during the January 2025 transfer window. But despite significant interest, a deal could not be agreed and Orjaester remained in Norway before eventually making the move to Twente.

Read more: Miffed Martin O'Neill bites back in Celtic BBC interview exchange

Celtic instead turned to familiar ground, bringing Jota back to Glasgow in a £10 million deal. However, the Portuguese winger suffered a serious setback when he picked up a long-term injury against Dundee United in April 2025.

That left the Hoops back in the market for reinforcements and, by the close of the summer transfer window, Michel-Ange Balikwisha and Sebastien Tounekti had arrived in a double deal worth around £10m.

Orjaester, meanwhile, was flourishing in the Netherlands.

The 22-year-old previously opened up on why he decided against a switch to the Scottish champions, insisting the style of football on offer elsewhere was a better fit for his development.

Speaking to De Twaalfde Man, he said: "I don't think the type of football played there suits me best.

"The Eredivisie has proven to be a very good platform for young players like me, and there are a lot of technically skilled players there.

"I didn't have much time to think about whether I wanted to go to FC Twente.

"Of course, I knew they were narrowly eliminated in the Europa League last season against Bodø/Glimt. Everyone I spoke to about the club talked about the fans and how Twente played."

While Celtic continue to wrestle with their current issues, Orjaester is producing the sort of numbers that justify the hype which surrounded him. And after rewriting the Eredivisie record books with a five-assist masterclass, the Norwegian has shown exactly why so many believed he could have been a star in green and white.

#2237. ‘Obvious candidate’: Tony Cottee names who he wants as new West Ham manager over Scott Parker

West Ham are in the hunt for a new head coach following their decision to part ways with Nuno Espirito Santo. WHUFC are positioned in 8th place in the Championship table after 13 fixtures and they are in the play-offs along with Wolves, West Brom, Southampton, Birmingham City and Stoke City.

Howe, 48, cut ties with Newcastle United at the end of July after just under six years in the North East. He is now weighing up his next move in the game.

Cottee, who had two spells with the Hammers during his playing days, wants the Buckinghamshire-born man appointed at the London Stadium and has said on talkSPORT: “The obvious candidate, the stand out, the best manager available at the moment is Eddie Howe, whose done a great job at Bournemouth and Newcastle. Could he come to West Ham? I think he could. Does Eddie want it? I don’t know. Is he looking at bigger clubs? I don’t know the situation. Secondly, you could go for a West Ham connection. I’m thinking along the lines of Scotty Parker, Craig Bellamy.”

West Ham are expected to turn to Scott Parker as their replacement for Nuno. He played for WHUFC during his playing days and has managed the likes of AFC Bournemouth, Fulham and Burnley in the past.

As Cottee, Howe would be an eye-catching coup for the Hammers if they manage to get him. However, it appears they have turned their attention to Parker instead.

Howe would also probably have reservations about dropping into the second tier. He has worked at Premier League level for a large chunk of his managerial career.

He guided AFC Bournemouth up the leagues before Newcastle United came calling in November 2021 after their takeover. He then got the Toon Army into Europe during his time there.

Assuming a deal is completed for Parker, he will be under immediate pressure to get West Ham promoted. WHUFC’s proposed new boss has done it before with Fulham, AFC Bournemouth and Burnley so knows what it takes.

A move for Howe is unlikely, despite Cottee’s desire to see him join the Hammers. He is likely to get a position in the top flight at some point down the line after the work he did at Newcastle United.

West Ham lost 3-1 at home to West Brom last time out in a result that proved to be the final straw for Nuno. They have slipped down to 8th and are clinging on to the final play-off spot amid pressure from the likes of QPR and Sheffield United below them.

They are back in action on Wednesday night as they aim to return to winning ways. They face a trip to South Wales to take on Cardiff City.

#2236. Allegri a SKY: “Siamo pochi, ci serve una gara di sofferenza. Prendiamo gol facili da evitare”

Massimiliano Allegri, allenatore del Napoli, ha parlato a Sky Sport alla vigilia del match di Champions League contro il Porto: “Infortuni? In allenamento non riusciamo a fare il torello coprendo il cerchio di centrocampo. Dobbiamo preparare la partita, è difficile perché il Porto è un’ottima squadra in casa. Noi dobbiamo fare una gara di sofferenza che credo ci serva anche. Mancano piccoli dettagli per portare a casa i risultati, la dimostrazione è l’alternanza di risultati che stiamo facendo in campionato. In Champions, indipendentemente da questa gara, il destino è nelle nostre mani. Con dieci punti si può andare ai playoff, dovrebbe essere un bel traguardo. In quei momenti ci vuole carattere, voglia di portare a casa il risultato in cui abbiamo lasciato tanti punti e preso tanti gol è una situazione di partita che va migliorata. Bisogno di sofferenza? Ogni tanto soffrendo un po’ serve, prendiamo dei gol troppo facili e questo non va bene, porta all’alternanza dei risultati. Rinforzi a gennaio? Pensare a quello che è successo e quello che sarà servito a poco. Vedremo cosa sarà. L’unica cosa che bisogna fare è andare in campo e giocare bene, la squadra ha fatfo buone partite in alcuni casi. Se prendiamo tutti quei gol negli ultimi trenta minuti vuol dire che non riusciamo a gestire alcuni momenti della partita. Non è questione di assenze, le assenze non sono una giustificazione. Dovrà essere una partita di sofferenza, siamo in tredici. Ci sarà da soffrire con una squadra che sta facendo molto bene. De Bruyne? Non è che non voglio dirlo, ma farà l’allenamento e manderò in campo chi sta in piedi”.

#2235. Liverpool boss in astonishing admission - I will urge my players to dive

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola says he will urge his players to dive in future after Alexander Isak was refused a penalty in Sunday’s 1-0 loss to Arsenal.

The Liverpool striker’s shirt was pulled by Jurrien Timber as he leapt to reach a cross into the box during the first half of the Premier League encounter at Anfield.

Isak did not go to ground and referee Andy Madley gave nothing. VAR Stuart Attwell also saw no reason to overturn the decision.

Asked if players should go down, Iraola said: “It’s a shame you ask me this question, but honestly, yes, we have to tell them, go down, because they’re not going to call it otherwise.

Read more: ‘Emotional’ Marink Reedijk enjoys post-match scenes as Hibernian book final spot

“And then referees complain why they go down. Because if you don’t go down, you don’t call it. Then it’s like, no, you are all the time going down.

“But I think Alex is honest. He tries to go for the ball, everyone can see live straight away there is a clear, clear pull.”

He added in a BBC interview: “The answer is you have to dive. If you don’t dive they are not going to call it.”

The incident occurred soon after Arsenal had taken the lead in the 16th minute as Kai Havertz benefited from an Alisson Becker error.

Liverpool went on to dominate for large spells but could not break Arsenal’s resilience.

Florian Wirtz did hit the bar from a free-kick and Cody Gakpo also had a penalty appeal turned down after a tussle with Christos Tzolis but Iraola was less concerned about that decision.

He said: “The Gakpo one, I think it’s a sustained holding but I understand their argument and I think they are right that they say the ball was too long and Cody wouldn’t have arrived to the ball.

“I think we have to blame the start of the game. Until we conceded the goal, (we were not) at the level of the rest of the game. But from 1-0, I loved the reaction of the team.”

Arsenal’s victory was their first at Anfield in the league for 14 years and took them to the top of the table.

Manager Mikel Arteta said the champions were motivated by a desire to bounce back from their shock Carabao Cup loss to League Two Fleetwood in midweek.

Arteta said: “It has been such a long time without having this winning feeling here.

“We are extremely proud of the team and the players and what everyone has done, especially in the conditions in which we arrived to this game – the defeat against Fleetwood looks the end of the world, but then you have to pick yourself up.

“How the hell can you go out of the cup when you shoot 27 times and have the chances we had against a team who had one shot on target? Then you look so silly but I had the feeling now was the moment.”

#2234. Decisioni del Giudice Sportivo: stangata Lazio e prima sanzione per Pinamonti

Decisioni ufficiali dopo il match dell'Olimpico: 3.000 euro di sanzione al club biancoceleste e prima ammonizione per l'attaccante

Con la conclusione dell'ultimo turno di Serie A arrivano i verdetti del giudice sportivo Gerardo Mastrandrea. Sotto la lente d'ingrandimento sono finiti i referti di tutte le gare, tra cui quella vinta dalla Lazio per 2-1 contro il Cagliari.

Il bollettino ufficiale riporta anche i cartellini gialli assegnati durante la partita, tra cui la prima ammonizione stagionale per l'attaccante Andrea Pinamonti, per essersi tolto la maglia durante l’esultanza al minuto 83’.

#2233. Achraf Hakimi, campione a Parigi. E plusvalenza perfetta per l'Inter di Suning

Giuseppe Marotta aveva portato Achraf Hakimi all'Inter per 40 milioni di euro. Un investimento improvviso e molto importante, in un periodo storico davvero delicato come quello del Covid che, poi, sarà la mazzata sui conti di Suning. Nel giro di appena un anno si è trasformato in una cessione da 67 milioni, garantendo una significativa plusvalenza, ma soprattutto ha permesso al club nerazzurro di far fronte a una situazione economica sempre più complicata. Uno dei momenti più difficili della storia recente dell'Inter, superato anche grazie alle cessioni di Hakimi e Lukaku e al prestito di Oaktree, che ha consentito a Zhang di reperire le risorse necessarie per andare avanti.

Hakimi, nel frattempo, a Parigi ha continuato a fare benissimo. Con la maglia del PSG ha collezionato 220 presenze e 31 gol, compreso quello che ha contribuito a indirizzare la finale di Champions League di Monaco contro la stessa Inter. Oggi è considerato uno dei migliori interpreti del ruolo, oltre a essere uno dei pochi giocatori cresciuti nel Real Madrid e poi lasciati partire senza avere davvero l'opportunità di affermarsi con la prima squadra.

La stagioni culminate con le vittorie della Champions League con il Paris Saint-Germain lo hanno portato anche tra i possibili candidati al Pallone d'Oro. Oggi Achraf Hakimi compie 28 anni.

#2232. ‘All of a sudden’: Sheffield United in strong position ahead of next three fixtures, says EFL expert

Sheffield United have risen up to 10th in the league after their first 13 fixtures and they are three points off the play-offs behind West Ham in 8th. SUFC won 1-0 at home against Wrexham last time out with Ben Brereton Diaz getting their goal.

The Blades are back in action on Tuesday evening with an away trip to Deepdale to face rock bottom Preston North End. They then face struggling Charlton Athletic and Watford.

Maxwell has delivered his verdict on the South Yorkshire outfit on the Not The Top 20 Podcast on YouTube: “Maybe the most impressed I’ve been with them this season (against Wrexham). That is quite a lot bar to clear I will say. (Romelle) Donovan looked good. I think increasingly (Michael) Cooper in goal, (Japhet) Tanganga and (Liam) Kitching at centre-back, (Sydie) Peck and (Kalvin) Phillips in midfield, it’s quite a nice spine.

“All of a sudden they’re up in 10th Sheffield United having had what felt like a really poor start to the season. They’ve got Preston next away and then Charlton away, after the break Watford at home so 10th right now with three fixtures on paper against teams right down at the bottom.”

On his day, Sheffield United goalkeeper Michael Cooper is one of the best players in his position in the division. He is then backed up on the bench by the experienced Adam Davies.

The Blades have been solid defensively so far in this campaign. Cooper has kept five clean sheets along with Stoke City’s Viktor Johansson and Birmingham City’s James Beadle, with only Swansea City’s Lawrence Vigouroux keeping more.

As Maxwell has alluded to, Japhet Tanganga and Liam Kitching have formed a solid partnership in the heart of defence. The latter joined from Premier League new boys Coventry City in the summer and he has made a positive impression.

Sheffield United have useful full-backs like Femi Seriki and Harrison Burrows who like to get up and down the flank. Further up the pitch, Kalvin Phillips, Sydie Peck and Oli Arblaster are all good options to have in the middle of the park.

Patrick Bamford is a proven goal scorer up top for Wilder’s side. They also have dangerous attackers including Brereton Diaz, Romelle Donovan, Tom Cannon and Tyrese Campbell at their disposal as well so the competition and depth is decent.

Despite not being able to spend much money in the last transfer window, Sheffield United still have a strong squad. SUFC also have an experienced manager in Wilder.

There is no reason why the Blades can’t push for the play-offs this term. They have a nice blend of youth and experience in their ranks.

They will need to be at their best to get a win against Preston North End, regardless of the Lilywhites’ position and poor form. No game is easy and Wilder will be aware that it could be a potential banana skin for his players.

#2229. Ally McCoist left in stitches as Derek McInnes makes Rangers admission on-air

Rangers hero Ally McCoist was left in stitches as Derek McInnes issued an on-air one-liner over his start to life as Rangers manager.

The Ibrox hero couldn't contain his laughter as the Rangers boss admitted he faced a rocky opening to his tenure in Govan.

Rangers had exited the Europa League to Jagiellonia Bialystok, then the Conference League qualifiers to Jablonec before a draw and defeat in their opening two league matches.

However, since then Rangers have gone on a run of 11 matches unbeaten, advancing to the Premier Sports Cup final with victory over Aberdeen at Hampden this weekend.

But McInnes hasn't forgotten the early struggles as he joked with Jeff Stelling and McCoist on talkSPORT on Monday.

In a quip in response to Stelling's introduction discussing the challenges in the early stages of the season, McInnes said: "You've underestimated that slightly rocky part I think!"

The live stream then cut to McCoist who was doubled over at McInnes' honest assessment.

McInnes continued: "When you get a new job, it's normally for a reason – nothing is normally perfect. We had lots of work to do, but underneath it all, I felt if we came out the window with a strong enough squad, then we could compete. That's where we are at the minute.

"We needed a bit of confidence. The run started up at Aberdeen, going 11 games [unbeaten], and we're pleased with what we're doing. There's still a lot of improvement [needed]. But as Ally knows, at Rangers, we need to keep winning.

"The noise and everything that comes with it when you're not winning makes things so much more difficult.

"But I'm delighted with the response of the players. The game on Saturday was another case in point. We were the better team, we created more chances, we look as if we're scoring, but it took us too long to get the winning goal. But when it came, it was a great moment for us, and we look forward to the final now."

On there being progress to be made by his Rangers side, McInnes added: "There has to be (more improvement to come). No team is perfect at this stage of the season, the season is still in its infancy.

"People are so quick to judge and assume this is how it's going to be, but it's so early on. There's loads of improvements to come from us, but that's the same with most teams.

"We're a very young team, particularly in the forward line.

"A lot of stats will back that up. Sometimes we could do with a bit more nous and an older head up there just to try and make better decisions. But the potential is exciting, and the reach of some of these players is evident. But we need to try and win as we search for that potential."

#2227. Ally McCoist reveals vital Rangers transfer advice for star man Olwethu Makhanya

Ally McCoist reckons Olwethu Makhanya should have no thoughts of leaving Rangers any time soon despite attracting attention with his outstanding start to life at Ibrox.

The South African defender has emerged as one of the club's standout performers since arriving from Philadelphia Union in a £3million deal. Comfortable at centre-back and capable of covering on the left side of defence, Makhanya has become a key figure in Derek McInnes' plans.

His impressive form has inevitably sparked talk of interest from elsewhere, but Rangers legend McCoist believes the 22-year-old is in the ideal place to continue his development and establish himself further.

Speaking to talkSPORT Bet Online Casino, McCoist said: "Pat Nevin generally talks an awful lot of sense, and he's spot on here. I don't think Makhanya should be in any rush to go anywhere.

Read more: Thelo Aasgaard receives glowing 'DNA' praise on Rangers loan exit

"He's had a very good start, though the weekend was maybe a little reminder that you don't get any easy games and you're a target.

"So, from that point of view, there's no doubt that with the way he's started, there will be clubs looking at him.

"But I would be advising him to stay for a while, get the job done, keep getting rave reports, and see where it takes him."

McCoist is also encouraged by the progress Rangers have made under McInnes and insists the club's ambitions should remain as high as ever despite their European disappointment.

The former striker believes domestic success must be the priority, with the Premiership title remaining the ultimate target.

He added: "I don't think anything has changed. I think Rangers have got to set out right now to win every domestic trophy they can.

"You have to be looking to win the league title, that is the most important one at the start of the season for a team like Rangers.

"The Cups I always say are a more than achievable bonus, but you've got to get the league title.

"That is still the priority for me looking at it, and the priority for most Rangers fans right now."

#2226. David Storch ‘delighted’ but urges ‘patience’ as Sheffield Wednesday appoint Dave Challinor

Sheffield Wednesday have named Dave Challinor as the permanent successor to Henrik Pedersen after the Dane’s departure in October. The 51-year-old takes charge of SWFC on a contract until 2030 with Clint Hill and Anthony Sweeney joining as assistant coaches.

The move has sparked excitement among the Hillsborough faithful, and chairman David Storch is “delighted” with the appointment too. However, the Owls chief issued a strong reminder of the need for patience as Wednesday rebuild.

In his first words on Challinor’s arrival, Storch said: “We are still at the beginning of an ambitious journey. Significant progress has been made in rebuilding the foundations of the club, but we recognise there is much more work ahead.

“Our ambitions remain clear, but our progress cannot be defined by the outcome of one moment or season alone. We must establish a clear footballing identity, consistent standards and a culture capable of delivering sustained success. That journey will require patience, resilience and collective commitment. Progress will not always be straightforward, but we believe Dave has the leadership, character and determination to help us achieve our ambitions.”

There is excitement over Challinor’s arrival at Hillsborough, and it is justified. The new Sheffield Wednesday boss led Stockport County from the National League to the top end of League One, and he was a hit in previous jobs at Hartlepool United and AFC Fylde beforehand.

After moving on Pedersen and bringing in Challinor, fans will set high expectations. The Owls sit 9th, so the hope will be that the new boss can deliver progress and lift them further into the promotion conversation.

However, Storch’s words emphasise the need for patience, and perhaps indicate that Challinor will not be judged on whether or not this season is a success. Success would be defined as a top-six finish at the very least by many, given the strength of SWFC’s squad, but it appears that the club hierarchy are not going to demand that in the immediate future.

Instead, Storch’s comments indicate that Wednesday want to build towards those heights with three goals: a footballing identity, consistent standards and a strong culture. It suggests a quick ascent is not what is being demanded or expected, which does conflict with the hopes of sections of the support after Pedersen’s sacking.

Challinor’s track record and availability meant he was viewed by many as a shoo-in for the Sheffield Wednesday job. His trajectory matches the one desired by SWFC, and he has the promotion credentials to his name to lead the club out of League One.

The Chester-born boss has done an excellent job of building cultures at his former clubs and this is a clear desire of Storch and the other decision-makers at Hillsborough. The chairman’s words indicate he will be given the time to do so with the Owls.

Storch’s vision is a long-term one, and Challinor will help him fulfil the goals set out as Wednesday rebuild after relegation and administration. The fans want results though, so time will tell if the new boss can satisfy everyone in a demanding job at a big club.

#2223. Un talento al giorno, Niko Ilicevic: il più giovane esordiente in Bundesliga

Niko Ilicevic, nato alla fine di ottobre 2010, è il talentuoso centrocampista offensivo dell’Eintracht Francoforte. Solo un giorno dopo aver compiuto 16 anni ha esordito in Bundesliga, entrando nei minuti finali della vittoria 3-1 contro l’Amburgo ed eguagliando il record di Youssoufa Moukoko come giocatore più giovane di sempre nella massima serie tedesca. Nipote dell’ex nazionale croato Ivo Iličević, è già un punto di riferimento nelle giovanili dei tedeschi e nella Nazionale Under-17.

Caratteristiche tecniche Tecnicamente è un mancino naturale, di quelli che usano il piede sinistro anche per salire sull'autobus, playmaker naturale avanzato con tecnica eccellente, visione di gioco e capacità di creare superiorità numerica. Mobile, elegante e capace di decidere le azioni, unisce qualità individuali a maturità precoci. Considerato uno dei prospetti più brillanti del calcio tedesco, ha davanti un futuro enorme.

#2222. Ally McCoist in public Rangers transfer plea to star man - don't go anywhere yet

Ally McCoist believes Olwethu Makhanya should stay at Rangers, despite his impressive start earning acclaim.

The South African defender has become a key player for the club since his £3 million move from Philadelphia Union.

He has impressed at both centre-back and the left side of defence, making him a vital part of Derek McInnes' plans.

His form will likely catch the eye of other clubs, but Rangers legend McCoist thinks the 22-year-old should stay put and continue his development at Ibrox.

Speaking to talkSPORT Bet Online Casino, McCoist said: "Pat Nevin generally talks an awful lot of sense, and he's spot on here.]

Read more: Celtic handed fresh agony as star who got away rewrites Eredivisie record books

"I don't think Makhanya should be in any rush to go anywhere."

He acknowledged Makhanya's strong start but reminded him that the weekend's performance was a reminder that there are no easy games and he is a target.

"From that point of view, there's no doubt that with the way he's started, there will be clubs looking at him.

"But I would be advising him to stay for a while, get the job done, keep getting rave reports, and see where it takes him."

McCoist is also positive about Rangers' progress under McInnes and believes the club's ambitions should remain high, despite European disappointments.

The former striker emphasised the importance of domestic success, with the Premiership title being the ultimate goal.

He said: "I don't think anything has changed.

"I think Rangers have got to set out right now to win every domestic trophy they can.

"You have to be looking to win the league title, that is the most important one at the start of the season for a team like Rangers.

"The Cups I always say are a more than achievable bonus, but you've got to get the league title."

McCoist concluded that while Makhanya's value may be increasing, Rangers is the ideal platform for him to continue building his reputation before considering a move.

#2221. Harry Redknapp says 46-year-old will be a ‘great fit’ for West Ham as managerial appointment nears

West Ham are expected to turn to their former player as their new head coach following their decision to part ways with Nuno Espirito Santo. WHUFC are positioned in 8th place in the Championship table after their first 13 fixtures of the season as they eye promotion back to the Premier League.

Parker, 46, cut ties with Burnley in late April and is available for work. He has been weighing up his options over the last six months.

Redknapp, who both played for and managed the Hammers, has delivered his verdict on talkSPORT: “Scott’s got a great record in the Championship and has taken teams up. He knows the club. He was a very, very good player. I took him from West Ham to Tottenham. Good lad. He’s a very astute manager. I think he’s a great fit for West Ham.”

He added: “He hasn’t got an easy job on his hands. Take (Jarrod) Bowen apart, there’s very few players there who would have got into too many West Ham teams over the years. They’ve got great support, it’s a big club that unfortunately needs a big lift now.”

Parker played 129 games for West Ham during his playing days. As well as WHUFC, he also had spells at Charlton Athletic, Chelsea, Newcastle United, Tottenham Hotspur and Fulham.

The ex-England international, who made 18 caps for his country, hung up his boots in 2017. He has since delved into the managerial world.

He started coaching at Spurs before returning to Fulham as their manager in 2019. He guided the Whites to promotion to the Premier League in 2020 before doing the same with AFC Bournemouth two years later.

The London-born man also got Burnley up in 2025 so he knows what it takes to get out of the EFL. He has also managed abroad following a stint at Club Brugge in Belgium before his switch to Turf Moor.

As Redknapp has alluded to, Parker has promotion experience and knows West Ham well already. He should be able to get the WHUFC fans onside.

The Hammers need to find some form as they look to claw themselves back into the top flight at the first time of asking. They are in the top eight along with Wolves, West Brom, Southampton, Birmingham City and Stoke City as they chase down the top two Middlesbrough and Swansea City.

They lost 3-1 at home against West Brom last time out and were poor against the Baggies. They are back in action on Wednesday night with an away trip to South Wales to take on Cardiff City as they aim to get themselves back on track and return to winning ways.

West Ham managed to keep hold of Jarrod Bowen in the last transfer window. He has been prolific so far this term but needs some of his teammates to step up now.

The London outfit will get the chance to bolster their ranks this winter. They will also have the opportunity to let some players head out the exit door as well in January.

#2220. Pancaro: “L'unica cosa che non deve fare la Lazio è quella di mettersi pressione”

Dall'avvio da record alla gestione della pressione: l'analisi di Giuseppe Pancaro sulla straordinaria partenza biancoceleste.

Giuseppe Pancaro, intervenuto ai microfoni di Radiosei, ha analizzato il super momento della Lazio: la forza del gruppo, i successi senza pubblico e la gestione saggia degli obiettivi futuri.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Come sto vivendo questo momento Lazio? E' una Lazio bellissima, non è un momento. Ventotto punti in 10 gare non è un caso. C'è del valore, grande merito da parte di Gattuso. Finalmente anche la soddisfazione per i tifosi che da anni non sognavano più e adesso stanno gioendo.

Ancora più sorprendente fare questi risultati senza tifosi all'Olimpico? Questo è un ulteriore merito di questo gruppo perché la difficoltà ambientale è oggettiva da anni. La sensazione è che loro ora non avvertano questo problema. Sicuramente giocare una gara come quella col Cagliari davanti a 13000 spettatori rispetto ad uno stadio pieno qualcosa toglie sempre. Questa squadra è talmente forte, concentrata, unita e compatta che riesce ad andare oltre.

C'è un momento in ogni stagione in cui ci si accorge che l'obiettivo postosi è cambiato. Quale sarà questo momento in cui magari dai 40 punti si passa a pensare ad una coppa europea? Gattuso in tal senso è bravissimo. L'unica cosa che non deve fare la Lazio è quella di mettersi pressione. Eventualmente penso se ne possa parlare in primavera, al momento fanno benissimo a giocare pensando ad una gara alla volta senza mettersi addosso pressione.

#2219. Porto-Napoli, le probabili formazioni: Allegri in emergenza, ruolo inedito per Lang

In un momento di estrema difficoltà, tra sconfitte e infortuni che si accumulano, questa sera il Napoli fa visita al Porto nella sfida valida per la quarta giornata della fase campionato di Champions League. Gli azzurri inseguono l’impresa in terra lusitana, di questo si tratterebbe vista la situazione di grave emergenza con la quale si presenta al cospetto dei campioni del Portogallo. Direzione arbitrale affidata a Michael Oliver. Calcio d’inizio alle ore 21.

In patria i Dragoni dettano legge da quando sedici mesi fa la squadra è passata nelle sapienti mani di Francesco Farioli: dopo aver riportato il titolo nazionale in bacheca, il giovane tecnico italiano è saldamente al comando della classifica anche in questa seconda stagione con ben 5 punti di vantaggio sui rivali storici del Benfica. In Europa però è ancora al palo: tre gare, altrettante sconfitte contro Manchester City, Betis e PSV. Ballottaggio Samu-André Silva al centro dell'attacco.

Scelte obbligate per Massimiliano Allegri, costretto a fare i conti con una lista chilometrica di indisponibili: certe le assenze di Badiashile, Di Lorenzo, Olivera, Lobotka, Neres, Alisson Santos e Spinazzola oltre a quella di Marianucci, non inserito nelle liste UEFA. Domattina verranno valutate le condizioni fisiche di De Bruyne mentre Hojlund è sfebbrato e dovrebbe partire titolare. Inevitabile o quasi quindi il passaggio al 3-5-2 con Lang schierato in un inedito ruolo di esterno a tutta fascia, per coprire il buco apertosi sulla fascia sinistra.

#2218. Rangers boss Derek McInnes brands Falkirk win over Celtic 'not really a shock'

Rangers manager Derek McInnes has stated Falkirk's win over Celtic was "not really a shock".

The Ibrox boss commented on the weekend result when he appeared on talkSPORT on Monday morning, as he hailed the work done by John McGlynn.

Ally McCoist had singled out McGlynn for praise for the job he has done at Falkirk - and McInnes joined in on heaping praise on the manager.

And he insisted it wasn't a huge shock to see Falkirk beat Celtic.

On talkSPORT, McInnes said: "The likes of John, you like to see good managers doing good jobs.

Clearly they lost a few good players, and that's normally the way. It's difficult to keep them - especially at a club like Falkirk.

"You just see a good manager doing his work well.

"Although it seems a shock Celtic getting beat there, but it's not really a shock when you see it's Falkirk that win the game.

"Falkirk are capable of that, and they did that a couple of times last season as well."

McInnes then backed his former club Hearts to be in the title hunt this season.

He said: "I do think Hearts will be title contenders again with the investment and size of squad they have got and the level of player they have got.

"I think Hearts will be up there again. It will be more of a surprise if they're not."

#2217. Veteran with 522 EFL caps backs Lincoln City 23-year-old for ‘a big future’

Lincoln City have fared fairly well in their first 13 games of the 2026/27 Championship season, sitting in 16th with 15 points to their name. The Imps spent on new players like Mikkel Ladefoged and Andrei Coubis in the summer, but among those to impress on the step up from League One has been Deji Elerewe.

Now, the 23-year-old centre-back has received high praise from defensive partner and EFL veteran Sonny Bradley. Speaking to the club’s official media, he said: “I recognised it before the first couple of weeks that he came in the door. I could tell straight away in training that he was a big lad. He was aggressive, he was ready to get stuck in and everything that he was asked to do, he could do comfortably.

“I recognised pretty early that he’s got a big future in the game. He’s had a great start to the season, but it’s just the start. With the mentality that he’s got, I’m pretty sure he’ll want to take it into the rest of this year and certainly into the second half of the season.”

Having made 522 EFL appearances across all three leagues, Sonny Bradley knows what he’s talking about when it comes to impressive young prospects. Lincoln City’s stand-in skipper has played alongside and come up against plenty of top talents across his storied career, so his praise of Elerewe comes as a glowing review.

After starting out at Charlton Athletic, Elerewe made a name for himself at Bromley and earned his move to Sincil Bank in the winter. He started encouragingly, but has really stepped up in the Championship.

Elerewe has played all but six minutes of the Championship campaign so far, locking down a starting spot. He’s among the league’s top 13% of centre-backs for defensive contributions (113) and ranks highly for his interceptions (21 – top 7%), aerial duels won (40 – top 11%) and touches in the opposition box (30 – top 4%).

The Imps ace has the physical stature and power to hold his own against big strikers and he serves as an aerial asset in both boxes. At 23, he is of the age and profile to kick on further and challenge himself at a higher level in the years to come.

Elerewe’s progress at his young age means that excitement over his future is more than justified. He has the physical profile to be a success at all levels, so it will be a case of rounding out his game both defensively and in possession to push to new heights.

Lincoln City will have the firm belief that Elerewe can become a high value asset in the transfer market in the years to come. He has quickly grown into an influential player at Sincil Bank, and that will bring admiring glances from clubs higher up in the food chain.

For now though, Elerewe will be focused on the task at hand with the Imps, where he is under contract until 2029. Alongside his own personal development, the goal for this season is to stay in the Championship, and the London-born defender can have a key part to play in that.

#2216. Martin O'Neill sent health plea from worried Rangers hero as Celtic rivalry parked

Rangers icon Ally McCoist has revealed he would hate to see Celtic boss Martin O'Neill suffer and reckons the veteran manager has earned the right to walk away on his own terms.

The Ibrox hero, who has long admired O'Neill despite their rivalry, admits his biggest concern is the toll management can take on the 74-year-old's health. While McCoist hopes close friend Derek McInnes can guide Rangers to title glory this season, he stressed he would take no pleasure in seeing O'Neill pushed out of Parkhead or forced to continue beyond the point where the job remains enjoyable.

The former Rangers striker believes O'Neill's decades of service to the game, and his achievements at Celtic, mean he deserves the respect to decide for himself when the time is right to step aside.

Speaking to talkSPORT Bet Online Casino, the 64-year-old said: "I think Martin has absolutely earned the right and deserves the respect to stay for as long as he feels right. I really do.

"I would hate Martin to overstay his time at Celtic, first and foremost for his health.

Read more: Rangers boss Derek McInnes brands Falkirk win over Celtic 'not really a shock'

"That's the most important thing, because I've always gotten on really well with Martin. Obviously I want Rangers to win the league 100 per cent, but Martin has more than earned the right to see things out for as long as he wants at Celtic, and that should be the case."

McCoist also concedes Europe's demands could yet play a significant role in the title race.

"I don't think for a minute Martin will say they're prioritising, but their level of performance in Europe has been extremely disappointing. I know they created one or two chances against Benfica, but Benfica were three-nil up and done.

"The performances in Europe have been really disappointing from Martin's point of view.

"I don't have any doubt that it could work in Rangers' favour not having those Thursday European games. Celtic are not allowed, same as Rangers, to get into any game other than expecting to win, particularly at home, whether domestic or European, the fans won't allow it.

"So there is added pressure on Celtic, of course there is. But Martin will be delighted with their league form. I noticed a lovely quote from him this morning where he said it was a fantastic result at the weekend, but if they get beaten on Thursday there'll be another crisis!

#2214. Furious Besiktas star turns on team-mates ahead of crunch Celtic showdown

Besiktas star Amir Murillo has slammed his own teammates ahead of their trip to face Celtic, after they threw away a two-goal lead.

Celtic welcome the Turkish giants in their fourth match of the league phase of the Europa League after suffering three defeats to Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo.

Martin O'Neill's side suffered a shock defeat at Falkirk at the weekend, but Besiktas slipped to six points behind league leaders Galatasaray after they blew a 2-0 lead to only draw against Kasimpasa.

And Panama international defender Murillo was critical of his colleagues, before this week's match in Glasgow.

Read more: The Martin O'Neill explanation that Celtic support won't accept after Falkirk

He said: "We didn't do what we needed to do after going two goals up. We lost our rhythm. We relaxed. And that's why we lost two important points. It's very disappointing because we play well at home, but seem to have a problem away from home and we need to improve in those games.

"We need to show these kinds of performances that we do at home to be challenging at the top of the league."

And Portuguese international stopper Tiago Djalo agreed that Besiktas have a problem on their travels. The former Juventus and AC Milan star said: "Unfortunately, we can't seem to win away games at the moment.

"The only thing we can do is work harder and improve. I understand the disappointment and anger from the fans."

#2213. Cardiff City’s injury struggles continue as Brian Barry-Murphy confirms new blow for attacker

Cardiff City face West Ham on Wednesday night, the league’s highest scorers. It marks another tough game in a challenging run of fixtures, and the Bluebirds will be without forward Isaak Davies after a new injury blow.

Brian Barry-Murphy confirmed to BBC Sport Wales that Davies will face four weeks on the sidelines with a hamstring issue. Unfortunately for the City boss, the Welsh attacker is not the only concern, with Perry Ng and Alex Robertson in need of assessment while Dylan Lawlor, Calum Chambers, and Callum Robinson have been out too.

Robinson has been omitted from the last three matchday squads, but the decision has not been expanded on since Barry-Murphy first said ‘certain standards’ had not been met.

Aside from a loan spell in Belgium, Isaak Davies has always played for Cardiff City. He joined the club when he was seven, making his professional debut against Middlesbrough in October 2021 and scoring his first goal against Preston North End in January 2022.

Fans have a natural affection for the player because of his affiliation with the club. However, he has struggled to make a mark on the first team for the most part, and that has continued this term.

Davies has only played 74 minutes of Championship football so far this season, and he is yet to score. His highest goalscoring season for the Bluebirds is six goals, compared to 12 scored in a productive loan spell with KV Kortrijk.

He’s had injury absences to deal with too, impacting his bid to find consistency. It will be hoped this latest blow does not result in an extended spell on the sidelines with four weeks the initial timescale.

Although the news about Davies is a blow, defensive injuries are more of a concern at Cardiff City currently. The Bluebirds will operate with Yousef Salech up front and have the option of Jack Moylan should he be required.

However, defensively, they are without Lawlor, Chambers and Bielik, amongst others. It meant Barry-Murphy had to utilise Joel Colwill and Ollie Tanner as emergency full-backs at the end of the 3-0 defeat to Wolves.

Despite their defensive injuries, City haven’t done too badly at the back in terms of their performances. They have conceded 20 goals, less than nine other teams in the division.

The Bluebirds will be looking to take advantage of their upcoming fixtures, with games against the likes of Norwich City and Preston North End on the horizon. They will be hoping their injury problems ease as soon as possible to give themselves the best possible chance of taking the points in those matches.

#2212. Rangers star called up by under-21 national team after being dropped from full squad

Rangers star Kim Min-su has been named in South Korea's under-21 squad instead, after he was dropped from their full squad.

The Ibrox ace made his international debut for his country last month and played in three friendlies against Ecuador, Uruguay and Venezuela and was an unused sub against Uzbekistan.

But that wasn't enough to see him included in South Korea's latest squad for their games against Qatar and Saudi Arabia later this month.

However, he has now been included in their under-21s squad for two friendlies against Mexico.

The squad doubles as South Korea's Olympic team for the football section of the Games in two years' time in Los Angeles.

South Korea Under 21s boss Kim Eun-joong said: "This is a good opportunity to gain practical experience against a strong team, Mexico.

"We will identify areas for improvement and take our competitiveness up a level."

Kim will travel to his homeland for the two games against the Mexicans at Cheonan on November 14 and a rematch against the same opponents three days later at the same venue.

#2211. Santos impresses in first Man Utd appearance but cannot prevent defeat by Wrexham

Andrey Santos made a bright first Manchester United appearance as they fell to a pre-season friendly loss to Wrexham in Helsinki.

Sam Smith scored the only goal with an easy finish six minutes before half-time, moments after heading against his own crossbar defending a corner.

United were without the players who have featured at this summer’s World Cup – including new signing Youri Tielemans – as well as Benjamin Sesko, but Michael Carrick put out a strong starting XI in front of 20,000 spectators in the Finnish capital.

Santos, who became United’s first summer signing when he joined from Chelsea at the start of the week for an initial £48m, took his place at the base of midfield alongside Mason Mount.

Speaking just before the match, Michael Carrick had praised the 22-year-old’s attitude, saying: “He’s settled in really well, he’s a fantastic character. He’s buzzing to be here, you can see that.”

The Brazilian’s first involvement was to clear the ball away after Tom Heaton failed to gather under pressure from Smith seconds into the game.

Santos was left on his backside by Lewis O’Brien eight minutes in but the chance came to nothing for Wrexham as the flag went up. More encouraging was his sliding block on O’Brien moments later and he soon settled in, showing a good range of passing and winning several duels in a busy display.

However, Phil Parkinson’s side, who played their first pre-season friendly against Wisla Krakow in Poland last weekend, were looking brighter and threatened again when Bailey Cadamarteri nicked the ball off Ayden Heaven on the edge of the box before the defender recovered.

United’s first chance was a Joshua Zirkzee shot that fizzed wide in the 24th minute and they almost went ahead when Smith tried to clear a cornerm but instead sent a header on to his own crossbar in the 36th minute.

Moments later Smith was on the scoresheet at the other end and it looked all too easy as he was left with a tap-in after O’Brien’s cross appeared to go through Harry Maguire’s legs.

Sam Smith with the winning moment 🤌🔴⚪️#WxmAFC pic.twitter.com/YzTvnzIpz6

Twenty-one of the 22 players were replaced at half-time, with only Wrexham’s Aaron James staying on, and Carrick sent out a side entirely composed of academy products, facing a decent test against a Wrexham side now including the likes of Conor Coady and Kieffer Moore.

United dominated the ball but struggled to fashion chances as the pace of the game dropped. Instead, Wrexham threatened with a low shot from Davis Keillor-Dunn but Radek Vitek made the save.

When Ethan Wheatley prodded Harry Amass’ cross goalwards in the 78th minute, it was their first shot on target, but Dan Ward made the save before holding a low drive from Shea Lacey.

Dan Gore hit the deck in the single minute of stoppage time, but his optimistic penalty appeal was waved away.

We knew it wouldn’t be perfect - that’s only natural for the first pre-season game - and the main thing is that everybody came through it in good shape. No injuries so we can move onto the next step next week.

[Andrey Santos] and Mason [Mount] did some really good things and connected really well. There’s loads of little positives to take. The sharpness at the top end will come as we move through pre-season.

I was really pleased with the second half team. They controlled the game really well against a team who aren’t easy to play against. The boys took responsibility and their quality; they can really be proud of themselves.

Man Utd appeal unsuccessfully for a penalty when Dan Gore goes over in the area. Seconds later, the referee blows the final whistle. Wrexham, who were under pressure for much of the second half, have held on to beat Manchester United in a muted pre-season friendly in Helsinki.

Sam Smith scored the only goal in the 39th minute, having headed against his own crossbar three minutes earlier. There were 21 changes at half-time, 11 for Man Utd and 10 for Wrexham.

Andrey Santos, part of an experienced first-half XI, had a decent debut after signing from Chelsea in the week. The senior players looked understandably rusty, and a very youthful replacement XI were more dominant than their seniors. But they struggled to create clear chances and Wrexham deserved their win.

Full-time in Helsinki 🇫🇮First pre-season minutes in the tank for 22 Reds ✔️

Wheatley finds the underlapping Amass, whose pullback is cleared a little desperately by Wrexham. Amass, still only 19, looks really promising at left-back.

Man Utd’s youngsters continue to press for an equaliser. They haven’t created much but the rest of their second-half performance has been impressive.

Ward makes another comfortable save, this time when Shea Lacey tries his luck from 22 yards.

The left-back Harry Amass beats his man and curls a cross that bounces towards Ethan Wheatley at the near post. He stabs it goalwards and Ward makes a comfortable save. Tough chance, though Wheatley did well to get across the defender.

Man Utd’s best move of the second half. Dan Gore runs onto a return pass from Shea Lacey and sweeps a low ball into the six-yard box that is held at the second attempt by Danny Ward.

Wrexham substitution Alex Moore replaces Aaron James, who was the only starter on either side to play part of the second half.

The first chance of the second half falls to Wrexham. After a neat move through midfield, Davis Keillor-Dunn gallops into the area and drives a low shot that Radek Vitek saves well with his legs.

Kamason is booked for a late tackle on Dobson. That looked a bit harsh, certainly in a friendly.

Wrexham - in a back five, heaven forfend - are defending well and keeping the opposition at arm’s length. Unlike Argentina, Man Utd haven’t really tried any crosses yet.

No attempts at goal in the second half, on or off target, from either team. But the young Man Utd side have played some purposeful stuff and have had around 66% possession.

No chances to report but the young Man Utd side have started well, dominating possession and playing with greater urgency than their elders.

And this is the youthful XI that Michael Carrick has put out for the second half.

Man Utd (4-2-3-1) Vitek; Kamason, Devaney, Armer, Amass; Collyer, T Fletcher; Lacey, Gore, Williams; Wheatley.

Wrexham have made 10 changes, with Aaron James the only survivor from the first half. This is their new XI.

Our second-half XI 👇🔴⚪ #WxmAFC pic.twitter.com/pechlNMwxJ

Manchester United begin the second half having made 11 changes at half-time. We’ll have the full teams shortly, all being well.

Wrexham lead after a low-key first half in Helsinki. Sam Smith scored to enliven a half of few chances. Andrey Santos was lively on his Manchester United debut, gobbling up the ground defensively and playing forward at every opportunity.

We should have very different teams - perhaps completely new XIs - for the second half.

39 min: Man Utd 0 Wrexham 1 (Smith) Sam Smith gives Wrexham the lead. It came from a well-worked throw-in on the left. Thomason played a one-two before slipping a crisp pass into O’Brien in the area. His precise low cross, through the legs of Maguire, gave Smith a tap-in from three yards.

Man Utd hit the bar Mason Mount’s inswinging corner from the left is headed against his own crossbar by Sam Smith, woh was off balance as he challenged Leny Yoro. That’s the closest we’ve come to a goal at either end.

Broadhead wriggles away from Andrey Santos on the edge of the area, but Santos snaps back at him and Broadhead curls over the bar.

Zirkzee pulls up gingerly after being caught by a Wrexham player. Looks like an in impact injury rather than a muscle problem.

Santos and Mount probe on the edge of the Wrexham area. A through ball is cut out and rebounds towards Zirkzee, who whistles a snapshot wide from 20 yards. Not a bad effort.

Patrick Dorgu’s shot is blocked on the edge of the area. United are starting to find a bit of rhythm after a slow start.

Cadamarteri surges into the area and is about to shoot when Heaven makes an excellent lunging challenge. Wrexham look more likely to score at this point.

Smith barges Andrey Santos over long after the ball has gone. A bit of a needless challenge, one that Santos did not especially appreciate.

Both teams look rusty, United in particular. Wrexham have been a bit more direct and slightly more dangerous in attack.

Andrey Santos loses the ball in midfield, leading to a one-on-one chance for Sam Smith that is well saved by Heaten. Smith was offside so it wouldn’t have counted.

That opportunity aside, it’s been a predictably quiet start - lots of passing in midfield from United in particular.

The new signing Andrey Santos makes an important interception after 40 seconds. Nathan Broadhead seemed to foul the keeper Tom Heaton in the United area, but play continued and Broadhead’s ball across was turned behind by Santos.

Wrexham, in their blue change strip, kick off from right to left as we watch.

Both teams line up for the usual pre-match formalities. Harry Maguire and Matty James, a former Man Utd academy player, are the captains.

We’ve been back in training 10 days and we’re taking it step by step. It’s great to be back at it again.

Andrey Santos is a fantastic character and he’s settled in really well. He’s buzzing to be here and he’ll do really well for us. We’re not expecting anything crazy special today - it’s a step, just get your eye in and get back on the pitch. I’m really looking forward to the progression he shows while he’s here.

Youri Tielemans is targeting more silverware after completing his £35m move to Manchester United.

Tielemans has signed a five-year contract at Old Trafford after United triggered his release clause at Aston Villa.

The Belgium international played a key role in helping Villa lift the Europa League last season, but pushed for the move to United after turning down the offer of a new contract in the West Midlands.

“The ambition from everyone at the club is extremely clear; we are all determined to push for the biggest trophies,” he said.

“Signing for such a special club feels incredible, it is the culmination of years of dedication since I first fell in love with football. I have had the privilege of experiencing success in the game and it has only increased my determination to achieve more.”

I’m not sure when Man Utd last played Wrexham in a friendly, but the most recent competitive meeting between the sides was in January 1995. It was three days after Eric Cantona tried to kick xenophobia out of football at Selhurst Park, so United’s 5-2 win was somewhat overshadowed.

Andrey Santos starts in what is a pretty strong United XI.

Lining up for our first fixture of pre-season! 🇫🇮Watch LIVE on MUTV ⤵️

Our first-half XI in Helsinki 🇫🇮🔴⚪ #WxmAFC pic.twitter.com/WrXbc2B7JQ

The World Cup final? Pah! The 2026-27 Premier League season is just over a month away, and Manchester United’s pre-season begins this afternoon with a friendly against Wrexham in Helsinki.

Man Utd have started many seasons with a whimper since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement 13 years ago, but there’s plenty of summer optimism around Old Trafford. Michael Carrick overachieved so spectacularly as caretaker manager that a full-time appointment became inevitable. Now all he has to do is maintain that league form across a full season while also juggling the Champions League.

United have filled part of their midfield void by signing Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa. Tielemans is having a post-World Cup break but Santos is part of a United squad that also includes Bryan Mbeumo, Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw, Mason Mount, Patrick Dorgu and Leny Yoro.

“Everything about Manchester United is special,” said Santos after signing for the club earlier in the week. “It is an incredible feeling to join a club that some of my biggest idols have represented. As a midfielder, I am really excited to have the opportunity to learn from Michael Carrick. He is the perfect coach to help me take the next step in my career and push to achieve my dreams.”

Wrexham have ambitions to play United in a competitive fixture sooner rather than later. They missed out on the Championship playoffs but will go again with a very similar squad.

“This is a great test for us, it really is,” said their manager Phil Parkinson. “As always, when we were in the other divisions we looked to these games as a test and this will be absolutely no different.

“The out-of-possession stuff becomes really important against the better quality teams. But as we’ve always done, we’re not just going to these games to stop the opposition.”

After 55 long days...It's a United matchday! 🇾🇪❤️
