#2210. 'I thought I was watching The Karate Kid' - top ref rages at Rangers VAR escape

Mark Clattenburg has called out Ryan Lee and John Beaton after insisting Rangers' James Penrice should have been sent off during the Scottish League Cup semi-final win over Aberdeen.

The former FIFA referee was left stunned after Penrice escaped punishment for a first-half challenge on Aremu Afeez before going on to set up Ryan Naderi's late winner as Rangers booked their place in the final at Hampden.

Penrice, operating in midfield alongside Nicolas Raskin, escaped punishment after missing the ball and catching Aberdeen's Afeez with a high, studs-up challenge near the halfway line.

Referee Lee opted against showing a card, while VAR official Beaton chose not to intervene.

Read more: Martin O'Neill sent health plea from worried Rangers hero as Celtic rivalry parked

The decision has come under intense scrutiny, with Clattenburg unable to believe Penrice remained on the pitch.

Speaking on the So Near, Yet So VAR podcast, he said: “I thought I wasn’t even watching football. I was watching my favourite, The Karate Kid.

“Listen, it’s more justifiable and easier to understand when the ball isn’t really that high. If you look at it again, the ball isn’t really there, and I think the player knows what he’s doing.”

Clattenburg went on to explain why he believes the challenge was impossible to defend.

He said: “I think he’s just decided he wants to catch his opponent high with his studs.

“And when you’re playing the ball, when you’re trying to play, you don’t go in like that. You would go in with your body. You would go in with your knee.

“You don’t go in with your studs and then make a clear movement with the studs towards an opponent’s ribs, hip, wherever we want to call it.

“I was surprised it wasn’t red. I’ve seen it in real time.

“For me, when it’s not a footballing action, then you can never support a player’s actions, and I think when a referee gives a red, then nobody can have any argument.”

Former SPFL referee Bobby Madden agreed with Clattenburg's assessment, with both officials adamant Rangers should have been reduced to 10 men.

The controversy was heightened when Penrice went on to have a decisive impact on the result, providing the assist for Naderi's 83rd-minute winner that secured Rangers' place in the final.

Aberdeen will feel particularly aggrieved given the match-winning contribution came from a player many believe should already have been dismissed.

Clattenburg and Madden are not alone in that opinion. Former SFA referee Des Roache has also argued that Penrice should have been sent off for the challenge on Afeez.

#2209. Under-fire figure eyed Leicester City boss Russell Martin for top Premier League job in 2024

Leicester City hired Russell Martin in the summer, bringing him in to lead their rebuild after relegation from the Championship. The LCFC boss has faced criticism for inconsistent performances and a frustrating style of play, but it wasn’t long ago that he was held in very high regard.

Martin’s work at MK Dons, Swansea City and in winning promotion to the Premier League with Southampton saw him build a strong reputation in the game. So much so, Manchester United sporting director Jason Wilcox – who worked with Martin at St. Mary’s – put him forward as a candidate to monitor when the Red Devils were considering their Erik ten Hag replacements in 2024.

Wilcox viewed Martin as someone to monitor and consider for the role in the future, rather than as an immediate option. This was shortly before the 2024 FA Cup final in May, so around the same time as the Championship play-off final, which the Saints won.

Wilcox moved from Manchester City to Southampton in 2023, stepping into a director of football role for the first time. He would hire Martin from Swansea City shortly after, and the two found success together.

With Martin as manager and Wilcox as a director, the Saints would win immediate promotion back to the Premier League. It saw the stocks of both surge, but the boss stayed put while Wilcox was tempted away to become technical director in a new-look Manchester United hierarchy, before seeing his title switched to director of football.

Neither have found the same fortunes since though. Martin was eventually sacked by Southampton as they sat bottom of the Premier League table, and a dismal 17-game spell at Rangers led to his next managerial opportunity coming in League One with Leicester City.

Wilcox meanwhile remains at Manchester United, but he has been under-fire for shortcomings in recruitment. Many supporters pin their continued struggles on him, and he was in the line of fire when defender Lisandro Martinez called out the club hierarchy too.

Managerial stock comes and goes, and few have experienced the highs and lows quite like Martin. His work in rebuilding Southampton and getting them promoted earned rave reviews, and rightly so.

However, he stuck by his playing principles on the step up to the Premier League, and it backfired badly. Some would argue he has never really recovered from that, with criticisms over his playing style following him to Rangers and Leicester City, and his willingness to speak up and stick to his guns while speaking to the press brings ridicule.

Despite this, he is still a young manager at only 40, and his CV shows how he can rebuild struggling clubs and build a philosophy for fans, players and staff alike to buy into.

Martin is trying to replicate his past success at Leicester City. He faces an uphill battle to do so, but that will not deter him as both he and LCFC fight to return to their previous heights.

#2208. Celtic Europa League rivals make shock decision to sack history-making boss

Celtic's Europa League opponents Torreense have sacked the manager who made history with the Portuguese minnows after they slumped to the bottom half of the country's second tier.

The Hoops face one of the smallest teams ever to play in the league phase of European competition later this month when they play Torreense.

The game will be played in Leiria, 50 miles away from their home of Torres Vedras, because their 2,000-capacity stadium is not suitable.

They made history last season when they defeated Sporting Lisbon in the Portuguese Cup Final under boss Luis Tralhao.

But they have sacked him and replaced him with former Estrela da Amadora manager Joao Nuno instead.

Torreense are languishing in 12th place in the Portuguese second division after a disastrous season so far domestically.

However, they made history when they won in Norway against Lillestrom in their opening game and were only defeated by Sunderland after an injury time goal.

They play Armenian outfit Ararat-Armenia this week - the only team behind Celtic in the table, on goal difference - before welcoming the Parkhead side at the end of the month.

#2207. Tuchel learns lesson as England clinch third place in 10-goal thriller

Was this evidence of England head coach Thomas Tuchel already learning lessons from the Argentina collapse? Let’s hope so.

With England on the ropes and in danger of throwing away a lead against France, Tuchel resisted the temptation to flood his team with defenders and was rewarded with a World Cup bronze medal.

England looked on course to secure an emphatic victory to clinch the nation’s best World Cup finish since 1966 and yet Tuchel was left with the exact same scenario that had gone so badly against Argentina in the semi-final.

Leading by four goals at half-time, England somehow went into the final hydration break of this bronze medal game with a single-goal advantage. This time, Tuchel steered England over the line by getting his late substitutions right.

Jude Bellingham stepped off the bench to cap a wonderful tournament for him with the goal that made sure England finished the World Cup in third place.

It may have resembled an exhibition match at times, with France failing to turn up in the first half. But England’s thrilling 6-4 victory will send Tuchel home from the United States feeling a little bit better, even though he is not yet off the hook for what happened in Atlanta.

The fact that success against France was earned with a Bukayo Saka hat-trick, as well as goals from Declan Rice, Ezri Konsa and Bellingham, will prompt more debate over Tuchel’s decision-making when it really mattered. Not least why Saka watched the entire Argentina game from the substitutes’ bench.

Tuchel cut a relaxed figure, changing his touchline attire to a casual white T-shirt and tracksuit bottoms. But his team meant business, as they raced into a stunning four-goal first-half lead.

Saka played like a man with a point to prove. He scored twice and produced the shot from which England won the corner for Konsa’s goal in the opening 45 minutes. Was this a message to Tuchel or simply the winger taking out his frustration on France?

France looked uninterested from the start and it was a loose Désiré Doué pass that gifted possession to Rice. As England’s captain for the evening strode forwards, Doué did not bother to track him and Rice curled a lovely shot into the corner of the net to give Tuchel’s team a third-minute lead.

It's a quick start from England! 🦁⚡Declan Rice fires home the opener in the third minute against France ⚽ pic.twitter.com/ID4u3rXOuM

Having been criticised for sending on three defenders against Argentina, Tuchel started with five attacking players on the pitch and just Rice in front of the defence.

Saka had a goal correctly ruled out for offside before his shot was blocked for a corner, from which England doubled their lead. Rice turned provider, as he sent in a perfect delivery that was headed past goalkeeper Mike Maignan by Konsa five minutes before the first hydration break.

The Three Lions double their lead! 🦁⚽Ezri Konsa rises highest from Declan Rice's corner to head home 🙌 pic.twitter.com/8BfI1LSDOQ

While Tuchel would have been delighted with his team’s start to the game, Saka’s influence raises just as many questions as answers.

Saka was the next England player on the scoresheet. He sent Marcus Rashford away on goal. Rashford’s shot was saved, but England kept the ball alive and Saka eventually found the back of the net via a deflection.

The Three Lions lead France by three goals! 🦁🔥Bukayo Saka finishing off a quick England counter-attack ⚽ pic.twitter.com/9SCfE3uH3v

England had been given much sterner tests by DR Congo and Panama, and yet Tuchel’s players deserve praise for capitalising on such a terrible first-half performance from France.

Ebererchi Eze could not have believed that he was given the time and space to turn and pick out Saka on the stroke of half-time. He did so superbly and Saka easily added England’s fourth goal.

🗣 "France are being taken apart by England!" Bukayo Saka scores his second for the Three Lions' FOURTH goal against the two-time world champions 🤯 pic.twitter.com/4RshXY692E

It perhaps summed up France’s mentality that Kylian Mbappé, who threatened on a couple of occasions in the first half, reacted to England’s fourth goal with what appeared to be a slight smirk.

Tuchel’s name had been booed by some of those, mostly neutral supporters, inside the Hard Rock Stadium ahead of kick-off.

His star has undoubtedly fallen as a result of the Argentina defeat and yet nobody could have failed to have been impressed by what his and his players produced in the first half on Saturday night, however bad France had been.

When Tuchel made a change at half-time, there was no Dan Burn sent on to try to see out a 4-0 win. Instead, it was an attacking substitution with Ollie Watkins replacing Rashford. It immediately backfired, but Tuchel was later rewarded for trying to remain positive.

Watkins’s first act was to lose the ball on the halfway line to start a France attack that ended in a goal. Michael Olise played in Mbappé, who slotted the ball past Dean Henderson, who was given a rare chance ahead of Jordan Pickford.

France substitute Bradley Barcola pulled another goal back in the 54th minute, which meant that England’s four-goal advantage had been halved in just nine second-half minutes.

There was still no call for Burn, as Tuchel stuck to his gung-ho approach and Henderson had to save well from Ousmane Dembélé, who had also been sent on at the break. England had lost their balance with the half-time change and Olise was the next France attacker to go close.

Dembélé tested Henderson again before Mbappé got France’s third goal just before the final hydration break to pass Lionel Messi as the World Cup’s all-time top scorer. Like they had against Argentina, England had dropped deep and invited pressure as their opposition grew in confidence.

Kylian Mbappe scores his 22nd World Cup goal to become the leading goalscorer in the history of the competition ⚽🔥👏 pic.twitter.com/sDTNnW0kLZ

Having led so comfortably at half-time, England went into the final quarter of the game with a slender one-goal lead – just as they had against Argentina in Atlanta.

Olise somehow missed a sitter after arriving late on the end of a low ball across the penalty area and Tuchel decided it was time for more changes. But it was Elliot Anderson and Bellingham he called for, rather than any extra defenders, and it ultimately paid dividends.

Bellingham almost dribbled his way through to put the result beyond doubt, before Olise squandered another wonderful opportunity. Mercifully, Djed Spence won an 85th-minute penalty that allowed Saka to complete his hat-trick.

Bukayo Saka completes his hat-trick from the penalty spot! ⚽3️⃣England lead France 5-3 in the closing stages of this game 🦁 pic.twitter.com/EnYOg8UAvT

There was still time for Dembélé to briefly up England’s anxiety levels again, before Bellingham put the finishing touch to what has been an outstanding World Cup for him with a brilliant goal.

Jude Bellingham grabbing England's SIXTH goal against France! 🦁Driving over the halfway line before firing a shot into the bottom corner 🔥👏 pic.twitter.com/l0B0BVs548

The players made sure to invite Jason Steele on to the stage to receive a medal. The Brighton goalkeeper is not in England’s World Cup squad, but travelled to North America as a training goalkeeper.

Of course I would love to have played more but it’s too late to talk about that. I try to do my talking on the pitch and it’s done now, move on. I’m fit.

We built and built across the tournament. We had some amazing results and in the end we fell short against Argentina. It hurts a lot to all of us and I’m sure it’s the same to the fans back home but we have to hold out head high and focus on the next one.

France are not hanging around for the ceremony. They are down the tunnel as organisers set up a stage to hand out the bronze medals. Probably sums up their attitude to the game.

Enough for four matches, what happened here. We had a brilliant first half, then a turbulent second half. You could see the difference of what one day makes and the difference in the schedule. We are so, so tired and drained from the last weeks.

So a massive compliment and full respect - the mentality that we showed. Going through all the adversity is absolutely brilliant.

I was afraid of the physical demands of the match. We know the quality and speed of France, and they have much less schedule for them. It was less demanding.

They had one more day in-between the semi-final to digest, and they had way less travel distances than us.

We played in the heat, at altitude. I was worried physically. You could see it in the second half, the cramps and all the tiredness, but I was never worried about the mentality.

I have said it before, this team has created something very special, and they showed it again.

However we got here England have had their best World Cup since 1966. Whatever criticism Thomas Tuchel received after Argentina defeat he deserves to keep his job and the chance to put things right in 2028 #england

Some players from France and England are huddled near the halfway line praying. Among them are Dayot Upamecano, Maxence Lacroix, Trevoh Chalobah and Bukayo Saka. Very different atmosphere to the Argentina defeat three days ago in Atlanta. They are playing Wonderwall here as they prepare for the bronze medals to be handed out but it is not very celebratory this time.

When does the second set start? That was as much as you could hope for from a third/fourth-place play-off. Some slack defending, some high-quality combination play and lots of entertainment. England’s victory stops things spiralling further for Tuchel, but there will be a sense of what might have been, not least the fact Saka played no part in the semi-final.

Bellingham’s seventh goal of the tournament, which is the highest tally by an England player at a World Cup. The game was stretched, but it was a fantastic individual goal from Bellingham, carrying the ball forward from the halfway line. He showed great composure not to take the shot too early, taking extra touches to finish with aplomb.

A seventh goal of the tournament for Jude Bellingham! 7️⃣⭐The most EVER by an Englishman at a single World Cup 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿👏 pic.twitter.com/YACnNWvqW1

Good work from Reece James to keep the ball and then defend well against Barcola.

What a barmy game this has been. Upamecano started the move with good defending and a surge forward, and then Dembele cuts inside Chalobah and buries a shot into the bottom corner.

🇫🇷 Ousmane Dembele scores France's fourth goal against England ⚽ pic.twitter.com/U4gCVb1tQw

Spence down and receiving some treatment for cramp after winning a challenge against Olise. France not happy with the stoppage in the game.

Excellent Rice challenge, and then Bellingham wins a free-kick in midfield. Rice can hardly run yet managed to time his challenge well. Trevoh Chalobah replaces Marc Guehi.

Seven minutes of added time to play, and France have just been caught offside from their own short corner.

That is England’s first World Cup hat-trick since Harry Kane scored three against Panama in the 2018 finals. But Bukayo Saka’s treble is also the last England hat-trick in all competitions since.... Bukayo Saka. The Arsenal forward also scored three times in the win over North Macedonia in 2023.

That was very unselfish from Jude Bellingham, because had he scored the penalty it would have been his seventh goal of the tournament. That would be the most goals scored by an England player at a World Cup.

Sends Maignan the wrong way, and picks out the bottom corner. Saka has his hat-trick, and England are surely assured of third place and the bronze medal/trophy. England’s players will be most pleased to avoid extra time.

Bukayo Saka completes his hat-trick from the penalty spot! ⚽3️⃣England lead France 5-3 in the closing stages of this game 🦁 pic.twitter.com/EnYOg8UAvT

Won by Djed Spence, who was too sharp by Malo Gusto. Once the England full-back got his toe to the ball, it was a stonewall penalty. Morgan Rogers played the pass to release him on the overlap.

Bellingham or Saka for the hat-trick? Bellingham has the ball in his hands, but then passes it to Saka for the hat-trick.

Qunsah off, Reece James on. That also looks a case of cramp in very humid conditions in Miami.

Now Olise misses a sitter! Great interplay in the box involving Olise and Dembele, five-a-side football between the France forwards, but the finish was lacking. Olise, and then the referee, receive some treatment for cramp.

England with a great chance to wrap the game up but Bellingham fluffed his lines! Burst through, the benefit of fresh legs, but he carried the ball too close to Maignan and then Rogers’s follow up was blocked.

Ivan Toney and Eberechi Eze are the players coming off, Bellingham and Anderson on, which adds some strength to England’s midfield.

That is a big cheer for Bellingham coming on, one of the stars of the World Cup and appreciated by the neutral. His job here is to see out a win.

France continue to dominate, and they have a free-kick in a crossing position. Cleared by Eze. Elliott Anderson is ready to come on, as well as Bellingham. Digne finds Mbappe, but Konsa makes a good block. Rogers then does well to make it stick and buy a foul.

Great chance for France to equalise, but Michael Olise opened up his foot too much and his shot flew past the post. France look like scoring every time they venture into England’s defensive third. Mbappe goes down looking for a penalty, but nothing doing, before Digne fouls Saka in the box. May have been knee on knee contact, looked a sore one for Saka. Bellingham is ready to come on.

Rice is still out there, soldiering on. Somewhat surprising that Tuchel has not added fresh legs since his half-time changes. Better spell of possession in the last few minutes from England. There have been 15 shots on target in this game.

Play has stopped immediately after the goal for the hydration break. Tuchel mist be thinking about changes. Rice is struggling.

A penny for Mikel Arteta's thoughts watching this: if one of his first comments during pre-season isn't an eruption about how Declan Rice has been asked to play again, he will have mellowed. He's as tired as an also ran at the end of the Grand National.

This is a fantastic France goal, razor sharp link up play between Mbappe and Olise at the edge of the box, and the France captain’s finish was unerring. Drilled into the bottom corner with his left foot. Liquid football. Defending remains optional in this game, but that goal would have graced any game. Mbappe’s 22nd World Cup goal.

Over to you Lionel! Mbappe’s 10th goal of the World Cup means he is the clear leader in the Golden Boot table - but Lionel Messi has a chance in the final tomorrow to add to his eight goals. You would not bet against Mbappe adding to his total here. England have been guilty of dropping deep again, just like they did against Argentina. They are a 4-4-2 with Ollie Watkins and Ivan Toney partnering each other. This was just before the “hydration”, so Tuchel could change it up now.

Kylian Mbappe scores his 22nd World Cup goal to become the leading goalscorer in the history of the competition ⚽🔥👏 pic.twitter.com/sDTNnW0kLZ

There is a loud chant coming from the stands: “Mexico!” That shows the diversity of the crowd here, with empty seats in sections including the England supporters. In just one small block of fans in front of the press box, there are shirts from Colombia, Inter Miami, Chile and USA.

France should probably be back to within one goal, but Ousmane Dembele scuffed his shot from a favourable position in the box and it was a simple save for Henderson. Then the goalkeeper pushes away a long-range hit by Upamecano.

Delightful scooped pass over the top of the France defence by Eze but Toney could not bring the ball under his spell off his chest. Then Spence does brilliantly to win a tackle and then turn defence into attakc with a surging run forward.

Morgan Rogers with a sloppy pass inside his own half, and Olise fires wide from the edge of the box. He had so much time and space to line it up. Some fatigue starting to show in England’s legs now.

This is what Tuchel was talking about when he discussed England playing under pressure. France have decided to show up and all of a sudden the deficit is only two goals. Get ready for a testing half an hour.

England go close to another set-piece goal, but Maignan saves well after Toney rose to meet Rice’s inswinging delivery. There are surely going to be more goals in this game.

Henderson stands up well to save from Dembele, but the flag belatedly was raised for offside. A lot of wasted energy for Declan Rice, who had sprinted back some 60 yards to defend. England now the team being repeatedly exposed in transition.

Mbappe with the ball inside Quansah, who loses track of Barcola and with his pace that is always fatal. It looked like Barcola might have overrun the ball, but he got his shot off in time to find the bottom corner.

It's a second goal for France! 🇫🇷Kylian Mbappe's long pass finds Bradley Barcola who fires home 🔥 pic.twitter.com/h4GvkBZOSN

Great play from Eze, close control and quick feet to skip through two or three France challenges in midfield, and he tried to chip Maignan from the halfway line. Always drifting wide.

Composed football from England, playing out from deep in their own half with Rice finding Rogers between the lines. Saka with a pass into Watkins but his shot was tame. Then England and Spence were caught forward, but Rice got his toe to the ball ahead of Olise. Then Rabiot volleys not far wide. Chances galore in this game.

France reduce the deficit through Mbappe’s ninth goal of the tournament. Watkins was caught in possession by Upamecano on halfway, and France found Olise free in the No 10 zone. Lovely through ball splits the England defence, and Mbappe finishes first time beyond Henderson with his left foot.

France hit back after the break! 🇫🇷💥Kylian Mbappe pulls one back with his ninth goal at the 2026 World Cup ⚽ pic.twitter.com/Hxfg1s46ER

Hernandez, Konate, Cherki and Doue off, Digne, Upamecano, Barcola and Dembele on for France.

Ollie Watkins replaces Marcus Rashford for England.

England will fly back home tonight with the feel-good factor of a win against a World Cup heavyweight but it would be foolish to think any of Thomas Tuchel’s problems are solved. In fact, Bukayo Saka’s two first-half goals only leads to the question: why was he left on the bench against Argentina? And Ezri Konsa for that matter. England did not lose a game that Konsa started and it was harsh to bench him against Argentina last Wednesday.

No frustration, I’m a little bit emotional, I can’t find the words to describe just how proud I am of these players. They are playing a game with broken hearts, I see 11 lads out there with broken hearts. I’ve seen them around the hotel the last few days, broken hearts. They can build a performance like that just through pride of playing for England, the team spirit we’ve built over the last seven weeks it’s been a privilege to watch. I know the cynics will say it is too late but we still play against a world class opponent.

4 - France have conceded four first half goals for the first time since a EURO qualification match against Yugoslavia in April 1968.WOW. pic.twitter.com/SePSwONNA8

Well, hands up who had this scoreline on their “bronze final” bingo card? A scarcely believable 45 minutes, and England have surely secured third place for this World Cup. There has been a lot to like about their attacking play, but for many it will make the frustration of Argentina sting all the more. France have been half-hearted in their defensive approach, but England have put them to the sword in style.

Just the four minutes of first-half stoppage time to play.

It is not a consequential game, but this is still a heck of a half from England. They are making mincemeat of a ragged France team. Eze with a lovely turn in midfield and through ball to his Arsenal team-mate Saka, and he found the bottom corner with an early finish. Four goals before half time.

🗣 "France are being taken apart by England!" Bukayo Saka scores his second for the Three Lions' FOURTH goal against the two-time world champions 🤯 pic.twitter.com/4RshXY692E

France are playing like they have been on the beach since their semi-final defeat by Spain last Tuesday. Tuchel won’t read too much into England’s best finish at a World Cup since 1966. He wants his team to perform under pressure and there has been none of that in this game.

Almost a fourth for England, Rashford’s low cross seemed to run under Toney’s foot when the striker would have had a tap in. Moments earlier, there was another great defensive recovery from Rice to block a Gusto pass.

Saka with a curling cross which is just beyond Rogers and drifts wide of the far post. France showing no signs of tightening up.

Breaking in behind this France high line has been like shelling peas for England. Saka’s pass initially released Rashford on the break, and he had plenty of time to think when running through on goal. Maignan saved, Saka’s rebound was blocked, but it feel back for Rashford who kept his head and picked out Saka who passed the ball into an unguarded net. Pretty farcical France defending.

That was a very close offside call from VAR for Saka’s goal. With Mike Maignan out of his goal, England needed to stay behind two France defenders. Marcus Rashford was about a foot onside before teeing up the third.

The Three Lions lead France by three goals! 🦁🔥Bukayo Saka finishing off a quick England counter-attack ⚽ pic.twitter.com/9SCfE3uH3v

Good save from Dean Henderson to deny Mbappe, who sat down two England defenders. You were waiting for the net to ripple, but his effort was too close to Henderson.

Then England break and Saka is in behind the France back four again, but his first touch is a little heavy, and he can neither get his shot off nor round Maignan.

England looking lively in attack again, Rashford with a delicious nutmeg on Zaire-Emery, before unleashing a swerving shot from almost 30 yards. Maignan was scrambling but he made the save. Rice then makes another ball recovery in midfield.

There is a bronze medal at stake but this match has the feel of an exhibition. There is no intensity to France’s press. Michael Olise is extremely hard-working usually but has allowed opponents to run past him. Players are only coming alive with the ball at their feet.

Quick feet from Mbappe inside the England box, but Declan Rice was well-positioned to win an important challenge. Half an hour into the game, and Mbappe is yet to nudge ahead of Messi in the Golden Boot race.

Guehi with a goal-line clearance after Mbappe squeezed a shot beyond Henderson, but the flag was up for offside in any case. It looked a close call on the replays, was a clever pass by Doue to find Mbappe. Henderson also did well to get something on the shot.

Play has now resumed, and England are back on the front foot after a Rice diagonal out to Quansah.

Time for the first hydration break of the game. Miami is one of the World Cup venues where it is probably appreciated.

You can only play the game in front of you, but England have done that well so far. They find Toney free in the box, but he cannot get his shot off on the swivel.

Mbappe laughing as we walks back to the halfway line, so France are not feeling too stressed, but England are 2-0 up in Miami. Good inswinging delivery from Rice, and Konsa rose highest on the six-yard line to glance a header into the far corner.

The Three Lions double their lead! 🦁⚽Ezri Konsa rises highest from Declan Rice's corner to head home 🙌 pic.twitter.com/8BfI1LSDOQ

Saka is causing France’s defence all manner of problems, this time Eze released him in behind the French defence. Lacroix did well to stick to his task and deflect Saka’s shot over the bar for a corner.

Marc Guehi sticks out a leg to block Mbappe’s low cross after the French forward dropped a shoulder and showed his burst of speed over a few yards. England defend the corner. The game continues to feel open, there’s more space for the attackers on the pitch than there would be in a semi-final.

Bukayo Saka has the ball in the net but the flag goes up for offside. Correct decision, he had just strayed a yard ahead of Hernandez. It was a crisp finish, cutting back inside and finding the bottom corner with his left foot. England finding it quite easy to get in behind France.

The entertainment continues: Cherki with a strike from the edge of the D, which was parried by Henderson before Spence hurried his clearance. Zaire-Emery picked up the loose ball but could not do enough with it.

He did not know too much about it, but an important recovery run from Spence enables him to get his heel to the ball when it looked like Mbappe was away. England continue to move the ball well, looking quite fluent going forward, which will only serve to frustrate fans further.

England flowing forward again, Saka in behind Hernandez and lifting in a cross that came all the way to Rashford at the far post. One touch to control, the second to shoot, but his effort was blocked, deflected behind for a corner. Rice’s delivery is too deep.

Mbappe with a shot inside the England box but it is blocked by the legs of Rice. This kind of game tends to be either soporific or care-free and entertaining, and it feels like this is going to be the latter.

That was Declan Rice’s first World Cup goal – and a beauty of a strike at that. It is still a strange decision to play him and add to his workload. This is not a game to judge Thomas Tuchel’s team on either, as France are not playing with urgency.

Doue with a sloppy pass across midfield when there was a chance for France to break, and Declan Rice intercepted. No France defender stepped out to engage the Arsenal man, and he was able to carry the ball forward unopposed. The finish was sweet, the ball was passed into the bottom corner from just outside the box.

It's a quick start from England! 🦁⚡Declan Rice fires home the opener in the third minute against France ⚽ pic.twitter.com/ID4u3rXOuM

The early indications are that Eze is playing in a deeper midfield position alongside Rice. Good pass from Dean Henderson into the free man Djed Spece behind France’s press. Then Rashford whips in a promising cross form the left towards Ivan Toney.

As expected, there are a fair few empty seats here. In the end where some England fans seem to be congregated there are blocks of green seats visible from the opposite end of the stadium. It could be quite a strange atmosphere with most of the supporters inside the stadium neutrals. There are a lot of Mexico and Colombia shirts.

For the penultimate time in this tournament, it’s time for the giant flags on the pitch and the anthems. Rice and Mbappe lead out their teams.

Tuchel booed when his name read out and picture shown at the Miami Stadium

This is a big evening for Dean Henderson making his first World Cup appearance. The Crystal Palace goalkeeper, 29, earns his sixth cap and an opportunity to stake his claim for the No1 jersey next season.

No, never [did he hesitate about playing them] because Declan gets more and more fit. He gets his fitness back and his health back and for Bukayo there’s no concerns. He didn’t start, he didn’t play in the semi-finals. He’s a key player for us and ready to go.

It’s just common sense. We have so many kilometres in the legs. We have so many travel kilometres in our bones. We have a day less recovery. We come from 10 men in altitude. We come from overtime here in Miami. These two guys, they gave everything physically in every match,. They were ready to go again but we keep them and have them to finish the match for us.

0 - This is England's first FIFA World Cup campaign to not see a Manchester United player feature in any of their games since 1958.Unused. pic.twitter.com/LN3L3e7q5q

We have to regroup, and we have to pick ourselves up and try to finish the tournament on a high.

I have always been hungry for this opportunity. It was frustrating. I only got a few minutes, but that is how football goes sometimes.

Now is my chance to prove I should have got more minutes. There’s a lot of goals in the team and on the bench.

Hopefully, we can bring goals, and hopefully we can finish the tournament on a win.

Thomas Tuchel has risked angering Arsenal by selecting Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka for this game. Rice has been recovering from illness and was running on empty for the last two games. He has also suffered neural pain in his hamstring and describes himself as playing “an obscene amount of games”. This is surely a chance to have a breather. Saka has been managing an Achilles injury all tournament and did not feature against Argentina on Wednesday.

2 - Declan Rice is the second Arsenal player to start a major tournament game for England as captain (World Cup/EURO) after Tony Adams at EURO 1996.Privilege. pic.twitter.com/MWlX7HiWXX

Seven changes to the team that was beaten by Spain, with Zaire-Emery starting in midfield. Rayan Cherki is preferred to Ousmane Dembele.

France XI: Maignan; T. Hernández, Lacroix, Konate, Gusto; Rabiot, Zaïre-Emery; Doue, Cherki, Olise, Mbappe

Subs: Akliouche, Barcola, Dembele, Digne, L. Hernandez, Kante, Kone, Kounde, Mateta, Risser, Saliba, Samba, Tchouameni, Thuram, Upamecano

Some of Tuchel’s regular starters do drop to the bench: Pickford, Kane and Bellingham the notable names. Slightly surprising that Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka both start given their ongoing niggles. It is a very attacking team with Rice sitting behind Morgan Rogers and Eze. Is Tuchel making a point there?

England XI: D. Henderson; Quansah, Konsa, Guehi, Spence; Rice, Eze; Saka, Rogers, Rashford; Toney

Subs: Pickford, O’Reilly, Stones, Anderson, Kane, Bellingham, Chalobah, J. Henderson, Burn, Gordon, Watkins, Madueke, Trafford, James

Kobbie Mainoo’s back injury means that he not only misses out today, but it also means he ends this World Cup without playing a single minute of the tournament. Ivan Toney gets his first start and you’d imagine Trevoh Chalobah will get off the substitutes’ bench at some stage for his first World Cup minutes. It’s certainly an attacking team, but it’s also a slightly strange one.

Our XI to face France 💪 pic.twitter.com/UexpADmHPr

Matt Law was one of the journalists in Tuchel’s absorbing pre-match press conference, and says he appeared wounded and possibly shaken. Matt writes: “There was some spikiness from Tuchel, when he deflected the odd question back to the reporter who asked it, and he was fidgety when not speaking, messing with the earpiece in front of him on the desk and twisting the wires. He did not look comfortable.”

The Morgan Rogers transfer to Chelsea means that two England players have moved for a British record fee during this World Cup.

Elliot Anderson moved to Manchester City for £116m and Rogers has cost Chelsea £117m. That means England have two players who have moved for a combined £233m during this tournament.

England vice-captain Declan Rice cost Arsenal more than £100m in 2023. I haven’t done the maths, but it’s fair to guess that England’s first-choice starting line up would be worth near enough £1bn.

He takes an excellent set-piece and his athleticism is to be admired, but do you ever see him dictate the tempo of a match in the way that Rodri will attempt to do for Spain when they face Argentina on Sunday in New Jersey? The blunt answer is no. He doesn’t have cute, clever balls in his armoury.

There was a bolt of lightning in the distance on arrival at the Hard Rock Stadium. The last thing this Bronze match needs is a delay to prolong the agony of this match. John Stones was distraught doing his pre-match media duties yesterday. It is harsh to ask players to get themselves up for this game after the devastation of losing to Argentina on Wednesday.

Morgan Rogers is on his way to Chelsea for a record £117m fee, in news which comes as a blow to Arsenal’s summer transfer plans. Rogers started the semi-final on England’s right flank and he is likely to be involved again tonight.

He leaves France having won a World Cup and reached the final in another. This team has arguably played the best football of the lot, but will finish empty-handed. The smart money is on Zinedine Zidane replacing him, who won three consecutive Champions Leagues while Real Madrid head coach. So he knows his way around knockout football.

Neither England nor France wanted to be playing this game in Miami, but they can have no complaints about the nature of their semi-final defeats.

Tournament favourites France were comprehensively outplayed by Spain, with their feted front four of Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele, Bradley Barcola and Michael Olise all turning in below-par performances.

England’s defeat by Argentina was perhaps not as much of a surprise, but the nature of Thomas Tuchel’s team’s second-half collapse was just as alarming as France’s no-show.

England’s manager was fiercely criticised for replacing Anthony Gordon with Ezri Konsa and switching to a back five in the 72nd minute, but Tuchel has since defended his decisions.

“If you are asking if I regret my decisions, if this is the question, then I say no. I don’t regret my ‌decisions because I ‌felt that we became ⁠too passive,” said Tuchel.

“I took several decisions, trusting my instinct, my intuition, my experience, trusting my competitiveness, and I took the decision in order to help the team and get the result.

“I would regret if I didn’t help. I would regret ⁠if we didn’t react, but I have no regrets over the decision itself.”

Quite how strong Didier Deschamps and Tuchel decide to go with their teams is anyone’s guess. There has been some suggestion that Mbappe will start to give him the chance to beat Lionel Messi to the Golden Boot.

Some of England’s regular starters, such as Declan Rice, look physically spent, so there could be some rotation, and even a chance for players such as Kobbie Mainoo who has not played a minute of football at the tournament.

The third/fourth-place play-off has been rebranded as the “Bronze Final” for this tournament, and Tuchel was keen to point out that finishing third would be England’s best World Cup result since 1966. They lost this fixture against Belgium in 2018, but the way that game has been widely forgotten speaks volumes.

#2206. West Brom begin talks over new contract for £1.5m star

West Brom named George Campbell as their new club captain in the summer following a stellar debut campaign from the American defender. Signed for £1.5m from CF Montreal in 2025, he has emerged as a key player for WBA.

Now, the Baggies are looking to reward Campbell’s success with a new contract. Reporter Mike McGrath says on X that the club are in talks over a fresh deal for the 25-year-old, despite the fact he is already tied down until 2029 as it stands.

Prior to the summer transfer window, reports stated that Campbell had interest from Scottish giants Celtic, amongst other clubs. A new contract would further secure the American international’s future at The Hawthorns in case admiration from elsewhere grows.

Campbell had impressed in the MLS with CF Montreal after coming through the Atlanta United academy. He has made the step up to Championship football brilliantly, swiftly locking down a starting spot last term and growing in influence over time.

The Pennsylvania native spent the early days of his West Brom career playing at right-back, but shortly after his caretaker appointment, James Morrison moved Campbell into his regular central role and it brought instant results. In the final 11 games of last season, Campbell started all at centre-back and WBA were beaten just once, keeping seven clean sheets along the way.

The American provided some key attacking contributions too, scoring the Baggies’ only goals in draws against Charlton Athletic and Sheffield United, and in a win over Bristol City.

Campbell’s emergence as a key player saw his leadership traits shine through, earning him the captaincy in the summer. He has retained a big role in Albion’s success this term, contributing to the joint-tightest defence in the league with 13 goals conceded while ranking highly for successful passes (694 – top 5% of Championship centre-backs) and successful dribbles (eight – top 3%).

A new Campbell contract isn’t a must because of the time remaining on his existing deal. However, it will play a big part in keeping him happy and fending off potential admirers.

Improved terms reflect his value in the side as West Brom captain and a standout centre-back. It means that any potential admirers will have to part with a pretty penny to try and tempt him away from The Hawthorns.

His club success has brought more opportunities on the international stage, starting in two USMNT fixtures over the last break. As Campbell’s stock grows, WBA know they have to keep him happy if he’s to stay for the foreseeable.

#2205. Jamie McGrath hopeful Hibernian heroics in cup clash can lift league fortunes

Jamie McGrath hopes Hibernian’s cup heroics can help revive their wobbling William Hill Premiership campaign.

Hibs went into the Premier Sports Cup semi-final clash against Hearts at Hampden on Sunday bottom of the league, having lost four out of four against their city rivals at the national stadium and with Marink Reedijk looking for his first win as boss at the fifth attempt.

It looked like another day of disappointment was on the cards for the Leith side when Jambos attacker Claudio Braga headed in from a Calvin Miller corner with only four minutes on the clock.

However, Hibs fought back and striker Martin Boyle deservedly levelled in the 19th minute and McGrath struck three minutes before the interval with his first goal of the season to ultimately set up a meeting with Rangers in the final at the national stadium on December 13.

Hibs are one point behind second-bottom Kilmarnock ahead of the trip to Aberdeen on Saturday and McGrath, 30, said: “It was a good feeling obviously to give back to the travelling fans.

“We haven’t given them too much to shout about so far this season, so I think they would have bitten your hand off for a win in Hampden against Hearts.

“But yeah, it’s obviously a great feeling, into a cup final now, so something to look forward to.

“Hopefully now this is the start of us getting a turn on things and building on that.

“We have to get our league form back on track because that hasn’t been good enough.

“I think over the last few weeks we’ve shown what we can do in spells.

“It’s just about getting a full 90-minute performance because even on Sunday we were probably on top for a large period of game.

“I know you can’t control the full 90 minutes, but we’re still adapting to what the manager wants and I think when you see on Sunday when it clicks, it can be really, really good, but it’s about keep working hard now.

“We have to build on these small details, Every day is something new for us to be learning and we’re heavily on the video clips and we’re all buying into it. So, yeah, we’re slowly but surely getting there.”

McGrath’s crucial counter after midfielder Joe Newell’s powerful low drive had been blocked off the line and the Republic of Ireland international quickly tucked the ball in at the near post.

He said: “The ball just fell and the next thing I know it was in the back of the net so I didn’t even know how to celebrate or whatever.

“It’s obviously my first of the season, so it’s been a bit of a frustrating period for myself with a few injuries and niggles and stuff like that.

“But hopefully now we can all kind of stay as fit as we can, the squad’s kind of coming back to full fitness over the next few weeks, so hopefully it’s all clicking at the right time.”

#2204. Fresh Oldham Athletic development sparks fierce backlash online

Oldham Athletic have had their appeals against Kai Payne and Kane Drummond's red cards in Saturday's defeat to Crawley Town rejected, which has not gone down well with the Latics fanbase.

Despite being tipped as one of the potential promotion contenders, it has been a poor start to the season for Oldham in League Two, and it was another frustrating afternoon for Micky Mellon's men against Crawley on Saturday.

Oldham had won just one of their previous nine league games prior to Saturday's meeting with bottom side Crawley, and their dismal form continued as they slumped to a 1-0 defeat to the Red Devils at Boundary Park, but the scoreline alone does not tell the full story of the dramatic encounter.

The Latics were reduced to 10 men in the 14th minute when Payne was sent off for a challenge on Danilo Orsi, and their afternoon went from bad to worse when Hammond saw red for a high boot on Kai Jennings just 16 minutes later.

Oldham battled valiantly despite their numerical disadvantage, but Crawley took the lead in the 52nd minute when Orsi bundled the ball home from close range after Charlie Barker to hit the crossbar, and they held on for just their second victory of the season.

The Latics currently sit 21st in the League Two table, and they are only outside the relegation zone on goal difference, but they have a chance to pull clear of danger when they face fellow strugglers Northampton Town at Sixfields on Tuesday night.

With many feeling that Payne and Drummond's red cards were harsh, Oldham submitted appeals against the decisions in an attempt to get their suspensions overturned, but it was confirmed on Tuesday that both had been rejected.

That means that Payne and Drummond will be unavailable for the game at Northampton on Tuesday night, as well as Sunday's FA Cup tie against League One side Sheffield Wednesday at Boundary Park and next Saturday's trip to Shrewsbury Town.

After returning for a third loan spell with the Latics this summer, Payne has scored one goal in eight appearances so far this season, while Drummond has netted two goals and provided one assist in 16 appearances.

However, Mellon will now be without the pair for three of the next four games, although they will be able to feature in next Tuesday's EFL Trophy clash at Barnsley as suspensions from the league do not carry over to that competition.

Oldham are not the only club to have failed in an appeal against a double red card in recent weeks, with National League side Carlisle United also having their appeals against Miguel Azeez and Harvey Bunker's dismissals in their 3-0 win over Harrogate Town last month turned down.

With plenty of Oldham supporters still feeling angry about the refereeing decisions in Saturday's defeat to Crawley, it is fair to say that the news that the appeals against Payne and Drummond's red cards had been rejected was not well-received, with many taking to social media to vent their fury in response to the club's announcement on X.

The incidents continued Oldham's long-standing frustration with referee David Rock, who sent off two Latics players last season, Ryan Woods and Mike Fondop, with the latter's red card later being rescinded after a successful appeal.

Should Oldham Athletic consider parting company with Micky Mellon after their poor start to the season? Tell us in the comments below!

Greater Manchester Police are currently investigating after video footage emerged appearing to show a fan throwing a crutch towards Rock as he was walking towards the tunnel, and Oldham supporters seem in no mood to forgive the official for his latest questionable calls.

After their appeals were rejected, there is nothing more the Latics can do to reverse Payne and Drummond's red cards, but one supporter called for Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who is known to be a passionate Everton fan, to intervene.

#2203. West Brom set for major boost - it will impact Celtic

West Bromwich Albion are plotting fresh contract action to secure the long-term future and reward the performances of a star performer at the Hawthorns in a new development which could have a detrimental transfer impact for Scottish giants Celtic.

The Baggies have undertaken serious strides in what represents James Morrison's first full campaign in charge, with the ex-Albion midfield star having guided his old side to safety in the dying embers of the previous campaign before directing a play-off charge this time around.

West Brom find themselves positioned fourth in the Championship ahead of this evening's crunch home clash against promotion rivals Southampton following three victories in their last four matches over Wrexham, Blackburn Rovers and title favourites West Ham.

An uplifting summer transfer window enabled supporters to dream of promotion pushes once again, and the Baggies did well to bolster Morrison's squad with influential signings such as Felix Horn Myhre, Jimmy-Jay Morgan and Rabby Nzingoula while retaining star performers in the Black Country.

It's no secret that a number of West Brom's players did attract interest, and one of those players to have earned admirers elsewhere is now edging closer to extending his stay in blue-and-white in what will come as a blow as far as Celtic are concerned.

The player in question is skipper George Campbell, who, as per a new update via X from Mike McGrath of the Telegraph, has been sought out for a contract extension by Albion.

Just this afternoon, McGrath has reported that West Brom have entered negotiations over a new contract for Campbell in an effort to reflect the three-cap USMNT international's ever-growing importance and authority at the Hawthorns after initially arriving in the summer of 2025 in a £1.5 million deal from MLS outfit CF Montreal.

Campbell enjoyed a positive individual debut campaign last time out in spite of West Brom's collective struggles, which would see the defender earn wide plaudits for his steely and composed defensive displays while racking up 39 Championship appearances and finding the back of the net on four occasions.

After being named as West Brom's club captain over the summer following Jed Wallace's departure, Campbell has taken his performances up a notch and has relished the added responsibility as the heartbeat of a much-sturdier backline under Morrison.

These five players won't be available when these two early pace-setters battle at the Hawthorns

That's exactly why the Black Country outfit are now pushing to secure a new contract for Campbell, who has appeared in all but one of his side's second-tier fixtures to date, and still has just under three years remaining on his current terms.

West Brom's ongoing contract negotiations with Campbell will represent a considerable boost to all at the Hawthorns if such discussions come to fruition, providing the Baggies with fresh security in the transfer market and protecting one of their prised assets from being poached while rewarding the 25-year-old with the sort of deal that his ever-increasing importance has only warranted.

It's not quite so much a boost for Celtic, however, with Martin O'Neill's side having reportedly expressed an interest in the ex-Atlanta United ace's signature at the back-end of the 2025/26 term.

Reports had suggested that Celtic were interested in Campbell alongside unnamed Bundesliga and Championship clubs, even indicating that the then-£2.5 million-rated Albion defender was open to the possibility of a switch to Parkhead.

It never materialised, though, and Celtic would actually last the summer transfer window without acquiring a central defender as O'Neill only made minor adjustments to his backline.

Type the top scorer next to each season. Surnames count. Two seasons had joint winners, so they need two names.

Indeed, the Hoops boss offloaded three central defenders while only bringing in full-backs Landon Emenalo and Jordan Lotomba from Chelsea and Feyenoord respectively right at the end of the window, and with the Glaswegian side's backline having been shakier-than-usual in league action with some notable gaping shortcomings in European competition, it's an area of the pitch that they will surely intend on bolstering once January rolls around.

However, should they seek to set their sights on a deal for Campbell once again, it's likely that any such efforts would go nowhere if he ends up putting pen to paper on fresh terms with Albion, whose ongoing efforts for a play-off finish could also go some way to convincing the popular captain of committing to a long-term future with the Baggies.

Naturally, West Brom supporters are excited by the news that a new contract for Campbell could be nearing.

Always keen for the club to keep hold of their star performers, it would be a statement of intent if the Baggies end up successful in their bid to extend the highly-rated defender's future and fans are lapping it up.

West Brom fans, how do you feel about this development with George Campbell? What should his valuation look like in the transfer market? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

It's not something you see too often, and it's only right that West Brom are intent on rewarding that importance and reflecting it through improved terms.

#2202. Wrexham consider Welshman as potential Phil Parkinson replacement after Championship rival snub

Wrexham have risen from the National League to the Championship under Phil Parkinson‘s lead. But now, the boss is facing questions over his future, with the Red Dragons sat 18th in the table after only one win in their last five.

And, as the North Welsh side look to come good on their big ambitions, a managerial change may await. A report from talkSPORT states that Rob Edwards is among the contenders to take charge of Wrexham if they decide to part ways with Parkinson.

The Welshman recently rejected the chance to take charge of Burnley, who appointed Fabio Celestini instead. Edwards has been out of the game since he was sacked by Wolves in June, and he is now keen to return to the dugout.

Edwards has become a well-known manager over the past five years or so, first rising to prominence by leading Forest Green Rovers to the League Two title. A short and unsuccessful stint as Watford boss followed, but the 43-year-old succeeded in his next job by taking Luton Town to the Premier League in 2024.

He left Kenilworth Road as the Hatters struggled to get over the hangover of relegation from the top flight. Middlesbrough offered Edwards his return to the dugout in July 2025, and his impressive work with a PPG rate of 1.81 ultimately saw him poached by Wolves after only 16 matches.

Edwards’ return to Molineux – where he spent time as a player and coach – didn’t go as planned. Nevertheless, he remains held in high regard for his strong Championship record, often leading sides who utilise attack-minded wing-backs with intense and direct football.

This style of play will appeal to Wrexham, who have set up in a similar way on their journey through their leagues. Edwards has Championship success and Premier League experience under his belt though, unlike current boss Parkinson.

Moving on from Parkinson will not be easy for Wrexham when that day comes. The 58-year-old has led their rise from the fifth tier to Premier League contention, and he has regularly received the public backing of owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney.

However, as far as successors go, Edwards feels like a great fit. He has stronger pedigree to try and take the Red Dragons to the next level, yet his similar success with wing-backs means he might be able to get results with the current squad of players right off the bat.

Furthermore, his Welsh citizenship is sure to please supporters who will be happy to have a compatriot at the helm.

Time will tell if Parkinson can hold onto his position, but as pressure grows, Edwards could be an ideal heir.

#2201. James Penrice expecting '10 times’ the joy if Rangers lift Premier Sports Cup

James Penrice enjoyed Rangers’ Premier Sports Cup semi-final victory over Aberdeen but believes the winning feeling will multiply by 10 if they win the final.

The Light Blues registered a 1-0 victory at Barclays Hampden on Saturday thanks to a late but deserved goal from striker Ryan Naderi, who pounced on a strike towards goal from Penrice to direct the ball into the net from six yards.

Gers players took the acclaim of their fans at the end after confirming Derek McInnes’ first final as boss, with Rangers facing Hibernian at the national stadium on December 13 after the Hibees beat city rivals Hearts 2-1 on Sunday.

Penrice, on loan from Super League Greece side AEK Athens, said: “I think it’s special seeing boys that haven’t seen the kind of scenes before, haven’t seen Rangers at Hampden.

“I think it can only help. And I think it will be 10 times that if you were to come back here and win it in six weeks.

“So the motivation for the boys is to relive that again, 10 times that.

“And I think that’s what we’ll be trying to put into the group and it can only help us.”

Penrice admits his decision to join the Ibrox side in the summer was vindicated – albeit there had been no hesitation.

The former Partick Thistle, Livingston and Hearts left-back said: “It was never in doubt. Never.

“It was the only place I wanted to go in the summer. And I pushed a hell of a lot.

“This is why I want to come here and play for a massive club and play in games like a final. It only backs up my decision.”

It was not a classic display from Rangers, especially in a low-quality first half but Penrice stressed the importance of digging deep to get results.

He said: “I think that’s what it is. We’d love to be knocking the ball about and score six or seven goals, but sometimes that doesn’t happen.

“Teams come and they sit lower and they make it hard for us.

“At Rangers, that’s going to happen. You need to score goals. I think it’s just that final bit. The final pass, the final shot. I think composure in front of goal. But I can’t complain.

“The boys ran themselves into the ground and I think big Ryan gets his striker’s goal and it’s a massive positive.”

Although he had been pushed into midfield at times in previous games, Penrice started alongside Nico Raskin in the Gers engine room in a tactical move by McInnes which raised some eyebrows.

However, Penrice took it in his stride, saying: “It was obviously not what I’ve been used to in a two. But when the gaffer says play there, there’s no question, I’ll play wherever.

“Whatever I can do to help the team is what I’ll do.

“Obviously, it’s not a position I’ve played in before in the past for Livingstone and Partick.

“But if he asks me to play in there, I’m going to say yes. I could play anywhere.”

#2200. Celtic Fans Collective demand Dermot Desmond attend AGM in person and face scrutiny

Celtic Fans Collective have called on Dermot Desmond to attend the upcoming Celtic AGM in person.

The supporter group issued a lengthy statement demanding that the Parkhead shareholder show up to the event in person to face scrutiny over boardroom decisions.

The group claims Desmond wields "considerable influence over the direction and decision-making" at the club and must "answer questions about his role".

A Celtic Fans Collective statement read: "For twenty years, Dermot Desmond has not attended Celtic's Annual General Meeting, despite wielding considerable influence over the direction and decision-making of our club.

"Although only a minority shareholder, Desmond appears to exercise influence far beyond his shareholding. With that influence comes a responsibility to be accountable.

"We call on Dermot Desmond to publicly commit to attending the 2026 AGM in person and answer questions about his role in the running of Celtic Football Club.

"Sending his son, another representative or a prepared statement in his place is no substitute for attending personally.

"The decision by Peter Lawwell to prematurely conclude last year's AGM left a clear impression among supporters that the Board had taken an opportunity to avoid scrutiny. Responsibility for how that meeting was conducted and ultimately concluded rests entirely with the Board.

"This year, however, the focus must be firmly on scrutiny rather than protest. There is a clear understanding across the support that the AGM must provide the opportunity for important questions to be put directly to those running the Club, without allowing scrutiny to be evaded once again.

"Celtic supporters have repeatedly sought meaningful dialogue and a more constructive relationship with the Club.

"At a time when fans want to see decisive leadership, a public commitment from Dermot Desmond to attend the AGM in good faith would be an important demonstration of his willingness to engage directly with supporters and shareholders."

Celtic Trust added: "As a Non-Executive Director of the Club, it is the duty of Dermot Desmond to attend the 2026 Celtic PLC AGM.

"He has been absent from these meetings for 20 years - refusing to face and answer questions from shareholders.

"He should commit to ending that absence this year."

#2199. New Sheffield Wednesday training ground footage has got Owls fans excited

Footage has emerged of new first team assistant coach at Sheffield Wednesday Antony Sweeney making a strong impression with the players at training.

Dave Challinor was officially appointed as the new manager by the Owls hierarchy earlier this week after the decision to dismiss Henrik Pedersen.

The Yorkshire outfit will be hoping that the 51-year-old makes a positive impact, with the club targeting a promotion push this season.

New owners Arise Capital have made a big impact since taking over at Hillsborough last May, and have overseen fresh appointments at CEO and sporting director, with Simon Wilson taking over in the latter role during the summer.

Wilson previously worked with Challinor at Stockport County, with the manager overseeing two promotions, as well as consecutive play-off finishes in League One in the last two campaigns.

He has brought Sweeney and former QPR defender Clint Hill with him as part of his backroom staff, with his first game in charge coming up this weekend.

Footage has emerged of new coach Sweeney addressing the players, emphasising the high standards that are now being expected under this new management staff.

With an authoritative voice, the 43-year-old claimed that straightforward passes into the channel will not be missed at Sheffield Wednesday, as he commands the attention of the first team squad.

“It’s a four-yard channel, we do not miss that channel at this football club,” said Sweeney, via Liam Norcliffe on X.

Sheffield Wednesday have confirmed Dave Challinor's contract and backroom staff after officially appointing him as manager

“We’re too good to do that, standards are higher.”

Sweeney previously worked with Challinor at Stockport, joining the club in August 2025 after their play-off disappointment in League One.

He was an important figure as a first team coach as the Hatters finished third in the table, again reaching the play-offs, as they lost to Bolton Wanderers in the final at Wembley Stadium.

The pair also worked together at Hartlepool United, and have reunited at Hillsborough alongside Hill, who was also at both of Challinor’s former clubs.

Is Dave Challinor the man to bring Sheffield Wednesday forward? Comment your opinion below

Sheffield Wednesday fans have all had a very similar reaction to seeing Sweeney’s demands about higher standards, suggesting it’s long overdue.

Supporters are excited by the prospect of this new coaching staff getting to work with the players.

The Owls will be hoping that the desire for higher standards will actually bear fruit on the pitch.

Standards was the key word that almost every Sheffield Wednesday supporter noticed from this new footage, highlighting where they feel the team needs to improve under this new regime.

Challinor’s first game in charge will come away to Oldham Athletic on 8 November in a 5.15pm kick-off.

The removal of Pedersen as head coach at Sheffield Wednesday is essentially the last remnant of the old regime leaving.

Challinor’s arrival makes him Arise Capital’s first managerial appointment, and means that this is now their vision for the future of the club.

Speaking about higher standards in training is the kind of strong first impression the new staff will want to make with the squad, and the fans.

But the proof will be in the pudding, and Sunday’s trip to Oldham will be everyone’s first opportunity to see if that can translate into improved performances and results in League One.
